In the first SpongeBob movie, SpongeBob sings “Goofy Goober Rock” while defeating Plankton.

On the Waterfront is a 1954 drama directed by Elia Kazan and starring Marlon Brando as Terry Malloy, a dockworker caught between loyalty to his friends and doing what is right. Terry works on docks controlled by the corrupt union boss Johnny Friendly, whose men use threats and violence to keep workers silent. Earlier in his life, Terry was a promising boxer, but the mob pressured him to deliberately lose an important fight, ruining his chance at a boxing career. He expresses his regret in the famous line “I coulda been a contender.” After witnessing the harm caused by Friendly’s organization, Terry must decide whether to stay quiet or testify against the boss, even though speaking out puts him in danger.

Black-and-white film shows images in shades of gray, from deep black to bright white, instead of using color hues. It was common in early cinema because color film was not yet widely available, but filmmakers still choose it today for its striking contrasts and ability to shape a film’s mood. The Tragedy of Macbeth, The Lighthouse, and Passing are recent examples. The Tragedy of Macbeth is a 2021 adaptation of Shakespeare’s play in which Macbeth murders King Duncan to take the Scottish throne. Denzel Washington plays Macbeth, and Frances McDormand plays Lady Macbeth. The film was directed by Joel Coen. It was his first feature made without his brother Ethan Coen, with whom he had co-directed films including Fargo and No Country for Old Men.

Howard Hawks was an American filmmaker whose career spanned comedy, crime films, and westerns. He directed the screwball comedies Bringing Up Baby and His Girl Friday, which are known for fast dialogue and chaotic situations. He also directed Rio Bravo, a western about a sheriff and his allies defending a town. In Hawks’s 1932 crime film Scarface, a ruthless gangster rises through Chicago’s underworld. It should not be confused with the 1983 remake, also called Scarface, in which Al Pacino plays Cuban drug lord Tony Montana. Hawks directed Lauren Bacall in To Have and Have Not and The Big Sleep, helping establish her tough-talking screen image. His films often feature capable characters who trade sharp remarks even when facing danger.

Video games are interactive digital entertainment played on computers, consoles, phones, and other electronic devices. Unlike a film, which viewers watch without changing what happens, a video game responds to a player’s actions, such as moving a character, making choices, or competing with others. Games can tell stories, present puzzles, or challenge players to work together or win a match. One well-known example is Fortnite, developed by Epic Games. It became especially famous for its Battle Royale mode: players land on an island, gather equipment, and compete until only one player or squad remains. Fortnite is also known for modes that let players build structures during matches, adding another way to defend themselves or gain an advantage.

The Prime Directive is a Starfleet rule in Star Trek that forbids officers from interfering with the natural development of alien civilizations. It is especially important when the crew of a starship encounters a society that has not developed advanced space travel: even if the crew wants to help, its actions could change that society’s future in unexpected ways. Star Trek producer Gene Coon is credited with establishing the rule for the series. It became a recurring source of conflict for Captain James T. Kirk and his crew aboard the Enterprise, because protecting people and respecting the Prime Directive did not always seem to lead to the same choice. The rule raises a central question in Star Trek: when is helping someone also a form of interference?

Euphoria is an HBO teen drama created by Sam Levinson. It follows Rue Bennett, a high school student in the fictional town of East Highland, as she struggles with addiction and reconnects with classmates. Their stories explore friendships, romance, identity, and the consequences of risky choices. Zendaya plays Rue, whose experiences are central to the series. Before Euphoria, Zendaya played Rocky Blue on the Disney Channel comedy Shake It Up, and she also played MJ in Spider-Man: Homecoming. Those earlier roles may help you recognize her, but Euphoria is a more mature drama that deals with difficult subjects, including substance use and troubled relationships.

“My Strange Addiction” is a song by Billie Eilish from her 2019 debut album, When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go? Its title compares an intense attraction to an addiction, while its lyrics include the line “My doctors can’t explain my symptoms or my pain.” The pop track also uses sampled dialogue from “Threat Level Midnight,” an episode of the television comedy The Office in which the characters watch a homemade action movie. Those spoken clips give the song a playful connection to the show. Eilish released another song from the same album, “Bad Guy,” which reached number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 when she was 17. If you hear the doctor lyric or the Office dialogue, the song is “My Strange Addiction,” and its performer is Billie Eilish.

George Lucas is an American filmmaker who grew up in Modesto, California, and studied film at the University of Southern California. He expanded his student short Electronic Labyrinth: THX 1138 4EB into his first feature film, THX 1138. He then directed American Graffiti, a 1973 coming-of-age film set over one night in 1962. It follows recent high-school graduates cruising their California town before some leave for college. Its cast includes Richard Dreyfuss and Ron Howard, and its rock-and-roll soundtrack helps capture the era. Lucas later created and directed the original Star Wars film, drawing on adventure stories and the idea of the hero’s journey. Star Wars became a huge success and helped establish the modern blockbuster.

The Office is an American sitcom filmed like a documentary, with characters speaking directly to the camera as they go about their work. It follows employees at the Scranton, Pennsylvania, branch of Dunder Mifflin, a fictional paper supplier. Their manager, Michael Scott, often creates awkward situations while trying to be funny and liked. Salesman Jim Halpert frequently plays pranks on fellow salesman Dwight Schrute, whose serious attitude makes their rivalry a major source of comedy. Dwight also grows beets on his family’s estate, where he runs a bed-and-breakfast called Schrute Farms. Guests can stay there for an unusual agritourism experience, combining a visit to a working farm with overnight accommodation. The show mixes workplace humor with the characters’ friendships and family lives.

Matt Smith is an English actor known for playing the Eleventh Doctor in the long-running science-fiction series Doctor Who. He took over the role from David Tennant and portrayed the Doctor as an energetic, eccentric time traveler. Smith later played Daemon Targaryen, a member of a dragon-riding royal family, in the fantasy series House of the Dragon. In the 2022 superhero film Morbius, he played the main character Michael Morbius’s longtime friend, who shares Michael’s rare blood disorder. This friend is known by the nickname Milo. After both men gain vampire-like powers, Milo becomes the film’s antagonist. These three roles connect Smith to science fiction, fantasy, and superhero stories.

The Chase is a British television quiz show in which contestants work as a team to win money while competing against a professional trivia expert called a Chaser. Each contestant first answers rapid-fire general-knowledge questions to build up a cash offer, then faces the Chaser in a head-to-head round on a board. If the Chaser catches a contestant, that person is eliminated; those who make it through add their money to the team’s prize pot. In the Final Chase, the surviving contestants answer more questions together and win the pot only if the Chaser cannot catch them. The long-running British version is hosted by Bradley Walsh, an actor who also played Danny Baldwin in Coronation Street and DS Ronnie Brooks in Law & Order: UK. The show has also had an American version.

Bill Murray is an American actor and comedian known for playing witty, sarcastic characters in comedy films. In Ghostbusters, he plays Dr. Peter Venkman, a parapsychologist who works with other scientists to protect New York City from ghosts. In Groundhog Day, Murray plays Phil Connors, a TV weatherman sent to Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, to report on the annual appearance of Punxsutawney Phil, a groundhog said to predict the weather. Phil discovers that he is trapped in a time loop: every morning he wakes up to the same song, “I Got You Babe,” and relives February 2. As the day repeats, he changes how he treats the people around him. The film’s title, Groundhog Day, is also the name of the holiday on which the story takes place.

BLACKPINK is a South Korean K-pop girl group made up of four members: Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé, and Lisa. The group is known for energetic pop and dance songs, striking music videos, and a large international fan base. In 2020, BLACKPINK released its first full-length studio collection, titled The Album. It includes “How You Like That” and “Lovesick Girls,” as well as “Ice Cream,” a collaboration with American singer Selena Gomez. BLACKPINK has also worked with Lady Gaga on the song “Sour Candy.” These collaborations helped introduce the group to listeners beyond K-pop. If you see the four members’ names together, or are asked which album contains “How You Like That,” “Lovesick Girls,” and “Ice Cream,” the answers are BLACKPINK and The Album, respectively.

Ratatouille is a 2007 Pixar animated film about Remy, a rat with an exceptional sense of taste who dreams of becoming a chef in Paris. Inspired by the late chef Auguste Gusteau and his motto “Anyone can cook,” Remy secretly teams up with Linguini, a young kitchen worker who cannot cook well on his own. By hiding under Linguini’s chef’s hat and guiding his movements, Remy helps prepare impressive meals at Gusteau’s restaurant. Their partnership is threatened by the discovery that a rat is behind the cooking, especially when the feared food critic Anton Ego comes to dine. Voiced by Peter O’Toole, Ego is deeply moved by Remy’s ratatouille because it reminds him of a comforting meal from his childhood.

The Stepford Cuckoos are a group of cloned mutant telepaths in Marvel Comics. Their members include Sophie, Irma, Esme, Phoebe, and Celeste. They were cloned from Emma Frost, a powerful telepath who was once the White Queen of the Hellfire Club. Emma can also transform her body into organic diamond, making her extremely tough. The Cuckoos often act and speak together because they share a telepathic connection, but each has her own personality and choices. They have appeared in stories about the X-Men, the mutant superhero team founded by Charles Xavier. In one story, Sophie dies after using a drug called Kick to help defeat Quentin Quire. Their shared origin is the key to remembering both names: the cloned sisters are the Stepford Cuckoos, and their genetic source is Emma Frost.

O. J. Simpson was an American football star who later became an actor and a major media figure. As a running back for the Buffalo Bills, he became the first NFL player to rush for 2,000 yards in a single season, reaching that mark in 1973. In the 1988 slapstick crime comedy The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad!, he played Detective Nordberg, a colleague of Leslie Nielsen’s bumbling detective Frank Drebin. The film launched a trilogy in which Simpson continued to play Nordberg. In the 1990s, Simpson was the central figure in a widely televised trial for the murders of his former wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ron Goldman. He was acquitted in the criminal trial, though a later civil jury found him liable for their deaths.

Orange Is the New Black is a Netflix comedy-drama based on Piper Kerman’s memoir about her time in prison. Its main character, Piper Chapman, is played by Taylor Schilling. Piper is a New Yorker who begins the series serving a 15-month sentence at the fictional Litchfield Penitentiary, a federal prison for women. Years earlier, she had transported drug money while involved with Alex Vause, a drug trafficker and her former girlfriend. That past relationship leads to Piper’s conviction and brings Alex back into her life at Litchfield. Although Piper’s story starts the series, Orange Is the New Black follows a large group of incarcerated women, showing their friendships, rivalries, personal histories, and daily routines. The series combines humor with serious stories about prison life and the people affected by it.

Joe Rogan is an American stand-up comedian, UFC commentator, and host of The Joe Rogan Experience, a long-running interview podcast. His career combines live comedy with broadcasting for mixed martial arts events, where he discusses UFC fights. On his podcast, Rogan holds extended conversations with guests from fields such as entertainment, sports, science, and technology. The show became one of the most prominent podcasts in digital media and was the most downloaded podcast in 2021. One guest was Ryan Holiday, the author of The Daily Stoic, who discussed ideas associated with the ancient philosophy of Stoicism. In August 2022, Rogan interviewed technology executive Mark Zuckerberg, then the leader of Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram. During the interview, Rogan joked that Zuckerberg sipped water “like a robot.”

Arthur Read is the main character of a series of children’s picture books and the PBS Kids animated show Arthur. He is an anthropomorphic aardvark, meaning he is an animal with human traits: he wears glasses, goes to school, and lives with his family in the fictional city of Elwood City. Stories about Arthur explore everyday challenges such as making friends, handling disagreements, and getting along with his sister D.W. The original picture books were written and illustrated by American author-illustrator Marc Brown, who also helped develop the television adaptation. Although Arthur shares a first name with the legendary King Arthur, the aardvark’s full name is Arthur Read.

Indiana Jones, often called “Indy,” is a fictional archaeologist and adventurer played by Harrison Ford in a series of action-adventure films. With his fedora and bullwhip, he travels to dangerous places in search of ancient artifacts, facing traps and rivals along the way. His theatrical debut was the 1981 film Raiders of the Lost Ark. In its opening scene, Indy takes an idol from a booby-trapped jungle temple and escapes as a giant stone boulder rolls after him. Later, he races a rival archaeologist to find the Ark of the Covenant, a sacred chest from the Bible. The film’s mix of history, mystery, and daring escapes helped make Indiana Jones a famous movie hero.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a Nintendo Switch adventure released in 2022. Kirby, the round pink hero from Planet Popstar, is swept into a strange new world filled with the ruins of a deserted civilization. As he explores its towns, buildings, and other abandoned places, he rescues captured Waddle Dees and battles enemies. The game introduces Mouthful Mode, which lets Kirby stretch around oversized everyday objects and control them. For example, he can become a car to drive through obstacles or use a staircase to reach higher areas. Kirby also encounters Meta Knight, a masked swordsman who sometimes acts as his rival. Meta Knight flies with batlike wings and fights using a sword called Galaxia; Kirby faces him in a Colosseum challenge.

Uptown Girl is an upbeat pop-rock song released in 1983 by New York-born singer-songwriter Billy Joel. Its narrator is a working-class “downtown man” who hopes to win the affection of an affluent “uptown girl,” even though she comes from a very different social world. The song’s catchy sound and story of a romance across class lines helped make it one of Joel’s best-known hits. In the music video, Joel performs among mechanics in a garage, emphasizing the narrator’s working-class identity. Joel is also known for Piano Man, a piano-centered song about a musician playing in a bar. Its patrons ask him for a melody because his music helps them feel better.

“abcdefu” is a pop breakup song by Gayle, a Dallas-born singer who released it as a teenager in 2021. It became her breakout single and an international chart hit in 2022. The title spells out the first letters of the alphabet before ending in “F-U,” expressing the singer’s anger at an ex-partner. Its music video opens with a red title card that says, “me and my friends visit my ex’s house (smiley face),” then follows them to the house. The song also has alternate versions: a “nicer” version changes the explicit wording to “forget you,” while an “angrier” version uses harder guitars. If asked for the song, the answer is “abcdefu”; if asked for its performer, the answer is Gayle.

Jorts is an orange cat persona who became famous through a viral workplace story in which someone tried to put butter on the cat to help him groom himself. The story also featured another cat, Jean, and inspired a social-media account written as if Jorts were posting. His name refers to “jorts,” or jean shorts, an item associated with University of Florida football fans. The account became known for posts supporting workers’ rights, labor unions, and people trying to organize at their workplaces. In particular, Jorts has voiced support for employees seeking to unionize at Starbucks, the Seattle-founded coffeehouse chain. Starbucks union campaigns drew national attention after workers at a store in Buffalo, New York, voted to unionize in 2021.

Aladdin is a Disney film franchise based on a folk tale commonly associated with the Arabian Nights, although the tale first appeared in a 1710 French translation of that collection. In Disney’s 1992 animated musical, Aladdin is a poor young man who finds a magic lamp containing a blue Genie. The Genie can grant wishes, and Aladdin’s adventures include a magic-carpet ride with Princess Jasmine set to the song “A Whole New World.” Comedian and actor Robin Williams voiced the Genie, making the character famous for rapid-fire jokes, improvisation, and celebrity impressions. Williams also starred in Mrs. Doubtfire and voiced the title character in FernGully: The Last Rainforest. Disney released a live-action remake of Aladdin in 2019, with Will Smith playing the Genie.

Taskmaster is a British comedy game show in which five contestants, usually comedians, compete to complete deliberately absurd assignments. They might have to eat as much watermelon as possible in one minute or find a way to get a camel through a tiny gap. The contestants often tackle tasks in different ways, so clever ideas and funny mistakes are as much a part of the show as winning. Comedian Greg Davies plays the Taskmaster: he watches their efforts, judges how well they did and awards points. Alex Horne, a comedian and musician who devised the show’s format, appears as Davies’s assistant. He delivers the assignments, observes the contestants and records their results before Davies decides the scores.

Stanley Kubrick was an American filmmaker known for his precise visual style and films that explore war, technology, and human behavior. He directed Dr. Strangelove, 2001: A Space Odyssey, and A Clockwork Orange. His 1964 film Dr. Strangelove is a dark comedy about the Cold War fear that a nuclear attack could destroy the world. Kubrick carefully oversaw the design of its imposing War Room set, where leaders debate how to respond to a crisis involving nuclear bombs and a Doomsday Machine. Peter Sellers plays several roles in the film, including the title character: a wheelchair-using former Nazi scientist whose arm repeatedly rises in an uncontrolled Nazi salute. By making a terrifying situation absurd, Kubrick shows how dangerous decisions can be made by flawed people.

Pizza Planet is a fictional, space-themed pizza restaurant in the first Toy Story film. Woody and Buzz Lightyear go there while trying to get back to Andy, and Buzz climbs into a claw machine filled with green, three-eyed alien toys. The aliens believe the machine’s claw chooses who will be taken away. After leaving Pizza Planet, Woody and Buzz ride in its yellow delivery truck, which has the restaurant’s name and logo on its side. That truck became a recurring Pixar “Easter egg”—a small detail hidden in the background for viewers to spot—in other Pixar films. So the restaurant in the claw-machine scene is Pizza Planet, and the vehicle Woody and Buzz ride afterward is the Pizza Planet delivery truck.

Master of None is a Netflix comedy-drama created by Aziz Ansari and Alan Yang. Ansari plays Dev Shah, an Indian American actor navigating work, friendships, and romantic relationships in New York City. After breaking up with his girlfriend Rachel, Dev travels to Italy in the second season to learn how to make pasta. The show mixes humor with questions about family, identity, and growing up. Its third season, released in 2021, shifts focus to Denise, a novelist played by Lena Waithe, and her marriage. Ansari also played Tom Haverford, an employee of the fictional Pawnee, Indiana, government in the sitcom Parks and Recreation. In that show, Nick Offerman plays Tom’s boss, Ron Swanson, a libertarian who dislikes much of the government work he oversees.

Clash of Clans is a mobile strategy game developed by Supercell, a game studio based in Helsinki, Finland. Players take the role of a village chief, building defenses and training troops while upgrading buildings such as the Town Hall. They raid other players’ villages to collect gold and elixir, resources used for further upgrades. Players can also join clans, which are in-game groups that work together and fight other clans in wars. A recognizable troop is the yellow-haired Barbarian, who appears on the game’s app icon. Supercell also created Clash Royale, a related game in which players use collectible cards to deploy troops and battle for towers in real time.

Abbey Road is a 1969 studio album by the Beatles, named after the London street where its cover shows John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr crossing at a zebra crossing. The album opens with “Come Together” and also includes Harrison’s “Here Comes the Sun.” Much of its second side joins short songs into a continuous medley, including “Mean Mr. Mustard,” “Polythene Pam,” “Golden Slumbers,” and “The End.” The final song on the first side is “I Want You (She’s So Heavy).” It grows from a bluesy refrain into a long, increasingly intense passage of repeating guitar notes and white noise, then cuts off suddenly instead of fading out. Another track, “Maxwell’s Silver Hammer,” tells a darkly comic story about a killer.

Francis Ford Coppola is an American director, screenwriter, and producer whose films helped shape modern cinema. He directed The Godfather (1972), a crime drama about the Corleone family, and The Godfather Part II (1974), which became the first sequel to win the Academy Award for Best Picture. He also directed Apocalypse Now (1979), a Vietnam War epic inspired by Joseph Conrad’s novel Heart of Darkness. Its scenes include helicopters attacking a village while “The Ride of the Valkyries” plays. Beyond directing, Coppola worked to give filmmakers more creative independence. In 1969, he and fellow filmmaker George Lucas founded American Zoetrope, an independent film production company in San Francisco, as an alternative to the traditional Hollywood studio system.

FromSoftware is a Japanese video game developer founded in Tokyo in 1986. It first became known for series such as King’s Field and Armored Core, which features battles between giant robots. The company later became famous for challenging action role-playing games, especially Demon’s Souls, the Dark Souls series, and Elden Ring. Hidetaka Miyazaki, its president and a game designer, helped shape the style often called “Souls-like”: players explore dangerous places, learn from repeated defeats, and overcome powerful enemies. Another FromSoftware game is Bloodborne, released in 2015. It takes place in the Gothic city of Yharnam, where a mysterious illness has turned residents into monstrous beasts. Players control a hunter who must survive a night of supernatural horrors.

Guillermo del Toro is a Mexican filmmaker known for dark fantasy stories that mix frightening creatures with human emotion. He directed the 2017 romantic fantasy The Shape of Water, in which a woman named Elisa falls in love with an amphibian creature. The film won the Academy Award for Best Picture. Del Toro also directed a stop-motion animated adaptation of Pinocchio, released in 2022. It is different from Disney’s live-action Pinocchio released that year. Another of his best-known films is Pan’s Labyrinth, a 2006 dark fantasy set in Spain after the Spanish Civil War. Its young heroine, Ofelia, encounters a mysterious faun who gives her a series of supernatural tasks. Across these films, del Toro uses fantasy to explore difficult experiences and the choices people make.

Thor is a 2011 Marvel superhero film about the Norse god of thunder. After Thor acts recklessly, his father, Odin, banishes him from the realm of Asgard to Earth and takes away his enchanted hammer, Mjölnir. Thor can lift the hammer again only if he proves that he is worthy of its power. On Earth, he meets Jane Foster, an astrophysicist played by Natalie Portman. Jane is studying unusual events in the sky when she encounters the exiled Asgardian, and the two grow close. As Thor faces danger on Earth and a struggle involving his brother Loki, he learns that being a hero requires more than strength: it also takes humility and a willingness to protect others.

Teletubbies is a British preschool television series set in a rolling green landscape called Teletubbyland. It follows four brightly colored characters with distinctive aerials on their heads: Tinky-Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa, and Po. The show’s opening features a sun with a baby’s face rising over a field, often with rabbits nearby. Episodes use simple stories, repetition, music, and playful sounds to entertain young children. The Teletubbies also have screens on their stomachs that show short clips of children in the real world. Tinky-Winky is the tallest Teletubby. He is purple, has a triangular aerial, and is known for carrying a red handbag. These details help distinguish him from the other three characters.

The D’Amelio family is an American social-media family best known for sisters Charli and Dixie D’Amelio. Charli gained a huge following by posting dance videos on TikTok, a short-video app owned by the Chinese company ByteDance. Her success helped make TikTok a major platform for online creators, while her older sister Dixie also became a prominent internet personality. Both sisters were associated with the Hype House, a Los Angeles-based group of creators who made videos together, before leaving in 2020. Dixie expanded into acting and music: she appeared in Attaway General, a Brat web series set at a hospital, and released the single “Be Happy” in 2020. Their parents, Marc and Heidi D’Amelio, have also appeared in the family’s online content and television projects.

Olivia Wilde is an American actress and filmmaker whose career spans television and film. On the medical drama House, she played Dr. Remy Hadley, a member of the main character’s diagnostic team who was nicknamed “Thirteen.” Wilde later moved into directing. Her first feature film as a director was Booksmart, a 2019 coming-of-age comedy about two high-achieving high-school seniors who realize they have spent most of their time studying. On the night before graduation, they set out to have some of the fun they think they missed. Wilde also directed the 2022 psychological thriller Don’t Worry Darling, which stars Harry Styles and Chris Pine. Her work on both sides of the camera has made her a recognizable figure in popular entertainment.

The Witch is a 2015 horror film written and directed by Robert Eggers, who later directed the psychological horror film The Lighthouse. Set in 1630s New England, it follows a Puritan family banished from their settlement to a remote farm beside a forest. When their infant son disappears, the family begins to fear that a witch or other supernatural force is threatening them. As crops fail and more frightening events occur, suspicion falls on the eldest daughter, Thomasin. In one disturbing scene, she tries to milk the family’s goat but draws blood instead. The billy goat, Black Phillip, becomes especially important near the end, when he takes human form and leads Thomasin to a coven in the forest.

House Targaryen is a fictional royal dynasty in George R. R. Martin’s fantasy world, known for its Valyrian ancestry and close ties to dragons. After Aegon I Targaryen conquered and united much of Westeros, his descendants ruled from the Iron Throne for generations. Some members of the family, including King Aerys II, became known for violent or unpredictable behavior often called “Targaryen madness.” Daenerys Targaryen, played by Emilia Clarke in the HBO series Game of Thrones, is another famous member of the house and is called the Mother of Dragons. HBO’s prequel series House of the Dragon focuses on the Targaryen dynasty roughly two centuries earlier, when a dispute over the throne between Rhaenyra Targaryen and Aegon II divided the family and led to civil war.

Zendaya is an American actress and singer who first became widely known on the Disney Channel series Shake It Up. She later played MJ, a classmate and eventual love interest of Peter Parker, in the Spider-Man films beginning with Spider-Man: Homecoming. On television, Zendaya stars as Rue Bennett in Euphoria, an HBO drama created by Sam Levinson. The series follows Rue and other teenagers as they deal with friendships, relationships, addiction, and identity. Its characters include Nate Jacobs, Maddy Perez, and Cassie Howard. In one memorable storyline, a school play includes a carousel scene that helps spark a confrontation between Maddy and Cassie. Zendaya also played Anne Wheeler in the musical film The Greatest Showman, which features the song “Rewrite the Stars.”

Arkham Asylum is a fictional psychiatric hospital in Gotham City where many of Batman’s enemies, including the Joker and Scarecrow, are repeatedly confined. Its backstory centers on psychiatrist Amadeus Arkham, who founded the institution after his mother Elizabeth’s mental illness; he later became a patient there himself. Staff members have included Dr. Jonathan Crane, the villain Scarecrow, who tested his fear toxin on inmates, and Harleen Quinzel, a psychiatrist who fell in love with the Joker and became Harley Quinn. The asylum’s troubled history is explored in the Batman graphic novel Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth, illustrated by Dave McKean. The title’s phrase “a serious house on serious earth” comes from a poem by Philip Larkin.

Battleship Potemkin is a 1925 Soviet silent film directed by Sergei Eisenstein. It dramatizes a 1905 mutiny in which sailors revolt aboard the Russian battleship Potemkin. Like other silent films, it has no spoken dialogue; instead, it uses title cards to show words on screen. The film is especially famous for its Odessa Steps sequence, which shows soldiers attacking a crowd and includes a baby carriage rolling down the steps. Eisenstein builds tension through montage, an editing technique that arranges shots in a rhythmic sequence. By placing contrasting images next to one another, he shapes how viewers understand and feel about the events. This idea is also associated with the Kuleshov effect, which shows that a shot’s meaning can change depending on the shots around it.

The von Trapp family is at the center of The Sound of Music, a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical adapted into a 1965 film starring Julie Andrews as Maria. Set mainly in Salzburg, Austria, the story follows Maria as she becomes governess to the children of Captain Georg von Trapp, a widowed former naval officer. The captain runs his household with strict rules, but Maria brings warmth and music into the children’s lives, teaching them to sing. As the family grows closer, Maria and the captain fall in love. Songs such as “Do-Re-Mi” and “My Favorite Things” help tell the story, while “Edelweiss” expresses the captain’s love for Austria.

Red Hood is a name used by more than one character in DC Comics. Jason Todd was Batman’s second Robin, following Dick Grayson, who later became Nightwing. The Joker killed Jason in the story “A Death in the Family,” but Jason was later resurrected and returned to Gotham as Red Hood. Unlike Batman, who refuses to kill, Jason is an anti-hero willing to use guns and deadly force against criminals. The name also connects him to the Joker: in one account of the Joker’s origin, told in “The Killing Joke,” the man who would become the Joker wore a Red Hood disguise during a criminal scheme at Ace Chemicals. He fell into a vat of chemicals there and emerged transformed. Jason’s choice of name recalls both his own death and the villain responsible for it.

Norm Macdonald was a Canadian comedian and actor known for his dry, deadpan delivery. From 1994 to 1997, he anchored Weekend Update on Saturday Night Live, presenting jokes in the style of a television news broadcast. In one bit, he repeatedly added “or so the Germans would have us believe” to statements, including one about German shepherds working as police dogs. Macdonald also played actor Burt Reynolds in recurring Saturday Night Live sketches called Celebrity Jeopardy!, a parody of the quiz show Jeopardy! with famous contestants. In those sketches, Darrell Hammond played Sean Connery, while Will Ferrell played the host, Alex Trebek. Macdonald died of cancer in September 2021.

Federico Fellini was an Italian film director known for movies that mix everyday life with dreams, fantasy, and striking images. His film 8½ opens with a dream in which a man struggles to escape a locked car in a traffic jam, then floats up into the sky. The scene introduces the film’s focus on a filmmaker’s thoughts and anxieties. Fellini also directed the black-and-white film La Dolce Vita, which follows gossip journalist Marcello Rubini through Rome’s celebrity nightlife. One of its most famous scenes shows actress Anita Ekberg wading into the Trevi Fountain. Fellini used scenes like these to explore fame and modern life while creating images that audiences remember long after the film ends.

Avatar Roku is a character in the animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Born in the Fire Nation, he was the Avatar immediately before Aang in a cycle of reincarnated guardians. Each Avatar can bend all four elements—water, earth, fire, and air—and works to keep balance in the world. Roku grew up as a close friend of Sozin, who later became Fire Lord, but their paths diverged when Sozin sought to expand the Fire Nation’s power. Roku opposed those plans, placing his duty as Avatar above their friendship. His animal companion was a tamed dragon named Fang. While Aang is often seen riding his flying bison, Appa, Roku traveled with Fang, who remained loyal to him throughout his life.

Star Trek: The Original Series is a science-fiction television show that aired from 1966 to 1969. It follows the crew of the starship USS Enterprise as they explore space, encounter unfamiliar civilizations, and face difficult decisions. William Shatner plays the ship’s captain, James T. Kirk. His first officer and science officer is Mr. Spock, played by Leonard Nimoy. Spock is half-human and half-Vulcan, and he values logic even when the people around him react emotionally. The crew’s adventures often raise questions about how to treat other societies. One important Starfleet rule, the Prime Directive, says they must not interfere with the natural development of alien civilizations. The series became the starting point for many later Star Trek shows and films.

Dolly Parton is an American country singer-songwriter, actress, and philanthropist. She grew up in a large family in rural Sevier County, Tennessee, and became a regular performer on The Porter Wagoner Show before building a successful solo career. Her best-known songs include “Jolene” and “9 to 5,” which helped make her one of country music’s most recognizable stars. Parton is also known for helping children learn to read. In 1995, she launched Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library in her home county. The program sends free, age-appropriate books to enrolled children from birth until they start school. It has since expanded far beyond Sevier County, giving families in many places a way to build a collection of books at home.

Captain America is a Marvel Comics superhero whose real name is Steve Rogers. During World War II, Rogers was a frail young man who volunteered for a secret experiment led by scientist Abraham Erskine. The experiment, called Operation Rebirth, gave him a super-soldier serum that made him stronger and faster; he was its only successful recipient. Carrying his famous red, white, and blue shield, Captain America fought enemies such as the Red Skull alongside his teenage sidekick, Bucky Barnes, a boy from Brooklyn. Near the end of the war, Rogers was trapped in Arctic ice and remained frozen for decades before being found alive. Bucky also survived the war, but was brainwashed and turned into a Soviet-controlled assassin called the Winter Soldier.

Bohemian Rhapsody is a nearly six-minute rock song released in 1975 by the British band Queen, whose lead singer was Freddie Mercury. Instead of following a typical verse-and-chorus pattern, it moves through a gentle ballad, a dramatic operatic passage, and a hard-rock section. Guitarist Brian May’s electric guitar solo connects the ballad to the opera-like section, where layered vocal recordings, called overdubs, create a choir-like sound and the word “Galileo” is repeated in high and low voices. The song’s influential promotional video opens with the four band members’ faces arranged in shadow as they sing, “Is this the real life? Is this just fantasy?” Queen also recorded “We Are the Champions” and “Another One Bites the Dust.”

Animal Crossing is a Nintendo life-simulation game series in which players make a home in a community of friendly, humanlike animal villagers. They can decorate and expand their house, collect and trade items, and build relationships with their neighbors. The games use Bells as currency, including for repaying loans on home improvements. Tom Nook, a tanuki-like entrepreneur, arranges those home loans and accepts the payments. In Animal Crossing: New Horizons, released in March 2020, players move to a deserted island that they can gradually customize. Tom Nook also oversees the island’s Resident Services, where players can get help as their community grows. Rather than following a fixed story, the series lets players set their own goals and enjoy everyday activities at their own pace.

Touch of Evil is a 1958 film noir directed by and starring Orson Welles. It begins with a celebrated long tracking shot that follows a car carrying a hidden bomb through a town on the U.S.–Mexico border. After the bomb explodes, an investigation brings a Mexican drug-enforcement official into conflict with Hank Quinlan, the veteran local police captain played by Welles. Quinlan has a reputation for solving cases, but he is corrupt: he plants evidence to make suspects appear guilty. The film uses dark shadows, tense scenes, and morally complicated characters, all features associated with film noir. Its border-town setting and twisting crime story make the question of whom to trust central to the film.

Vertigo is Alfred Hitchcock’s 1958 psychological thriller starring James Stewart as John “Scottie” Ferguson, a former San Francisco detective who fears heights. Shipbuilder Gavin Elster hires Scottie to follow his wife, Madeleine Elster, whose strange behavior seems connected to Carlotta Valdes, a woman from the past. Scottie trails Madeleine through the city, including a museum and a cemetery, and rescues her after she jumps into San Francisco Bay near the Golden Gate Bridge. He falls in love with her, but his fear of heights prevents him from reaching her when she runs up a mission bell tower and appears to fall to her death. Later, Scottie’s obsession leads him to discover that he was drawn into a carefully planned deception.

Redbox was a video-rental company best known for its red, self-service kiosks. These compact, unattended machines were often placed in grocery stores, gas stations, and pharmacies, where customers could choose a movie, pay to rent its disc, and return it later. A kiosk is a small station that lets people complete a transaction without help from a store employee. Redbox offered a convenient alternative to visiting a traditional video-rental store such as Blockbuster. It also differed from Netflix’s early rental service, which sent DVDs to customers through the mail in red envelopes. Both were ways to rent movies before streaming became the main way many people watched them.

The Daily Wire is an American conservative digital media company founded in 2015 by commentator Ben Shapiro and filmmakers Jeremy Boreing and Caleb Robinson. It publishes news and opinion pieces and produces podcasts and videos that discuss politics, culture, and current events, often from a conservative point of view. Shapiro is one of the company’s best-known figures. Before co-founding The Daily Wire, he became the youngest nationally syndicated columnist in the United States at age 17, meaning his writing appeared in newspapers across the country. He also wrote the novel True Allegiance and is known for the phrase “facts don’t care about your feelings.” These clues help identify both the company, The Daily Wire, and its co-founder Ben Shapiro.

Dance Dance Revolution is a rhythm game series that first appeared in Japanese arcades in 1998. Developed and published by the Japanese video-game company Konami, it challenges players to move in time with music. Arrows scroll upward on a screen, and players step on matching directional panels—up, down, left, or right—when the arrows reach their targets. The game judges how accurately each step matches the beat, making both timing and footwork important. Home versions brought the arcade-style floor-pad controller to video-game consoles, so people could play in their living rooms. Dance Dance Revolution belongs to the same broad genre of rhythm games as osu! and Beat Saber, though each uses a different way to interact with music. Konami is also known for the Metal Gear and Castlevania franchises.

The Academy Awards, also called the Oscars, are annual honors for achievements in filmmaking. They are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, and winners receive golden statuettes known as Oscars. Awards recognize many kinds of film work, including acting, writing, directing, and technical achievements. Two major categories are Best Picture, which honors a film, and Best Director, which honors the person who directed it. In 2010, Kathryn Bigelow became the first woman to win the Best Director Oscar. She won for The Hurt Locker, a drama set during the Iraq War. Bigelow later directed Zero Dark Thirty, a 2012 film that received a Best Picture nomination and sparked debate over its depiction of CIA torture tactics.

Attack on Titan is a Japanese manga and anime series about Eren Jaeger and humanity’s struggle against Titans, giant humanoid beings that threaten the surviving population. Most people live inside three enormous concentric walls: Wall Maria on the outside, Wall Rose in the middle, and Wall Sina at the center. In the year 845, a Titan breached Wall Maria at the district of Shiganshina, allowing Titans to enter and forcing many people to flee inward. Eren later joins the Scout Regiment, whose soldiers venture beyond the walls to fight Titans and learn more about them. They use specialized omni-directional mobility (ODM) gear to move through the air and strike a Titan’s vulnerable nape, at the back of its neck.

Stairway to Heaven is a multipart rock song by the British band Led Zeppelin, released on its untitled fourth album in 1971. It begins with a quiet acoustic passage, then gradually grows louder and more intense, ending in a hard-rock climax. Near that climax is an extended electric-guitar solo played by Jimmy Page, who wrote the song’s music and produced the album. Robert Plant wrote the lyrics and sang them. The opening lines describe “a lady who’s sure all that glitters is gold” and is “buying a stairway to heaven.” Her belief that wealth can purchase a path to spiritual salvation is a central image of the song. Its shift from gentle music to powerful rock has made it one of Led Zeppelin’s best-known recordings.

Fallout is a role-playing video game series set in an alternate future after nuclear war devastates the United States. Its world has a retrofuturistic style: people once imagined advanced technology while keeping the fashions and culture of the 1950s. Some survivors sheltered in numbered underground Vaults, and players often explore the dangerous wastelands beyond them. Different games take place in regions such as the Capital Wasteland around Washington, D.C., the Mojave Desert in Fallout: New Vegas, and the Commonwealth around Boston in Fallout 4. Along the way, players meet groups such as the Brotherhood of Steel and companions such as the dog Dogmeat. An iconic piece of equipment is the Pip-Boy, a wrist-worn computer used to check a character’s status and inventory, view maps, and manage equipment.

Hasan Minhaj is an Indian American comedian and television host known for using humor to explain politics and current events. He became a correspondent on The Daily Show, working during the tenures of hosts Jon Stewart and Trevor Noah. He later hosted Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj, a weekly Netflix series that combined jokes with reporting on political and social issues. In 2017, Minhaj gave the featured comedic address at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, an annual Washington gathering of journalists, political figures, and guests. Speakers at the dinner often use satire to comment on the news and the president. Minhaj joked about then-president Donald Trump, calling him the “liar in chief.”

Back in Black is a 1980 studio album by the Australian rock band AC/DC. It was released after the death of the band’s original lead singer, Bon Scott, and was their first studio record with new vocalist Brian Johnson. Johnson sang lead on songs including “You Shook Me All Night Long,” one of the album’s best-known tracks. Other songs include “Hells Bells” and the title track, “Back in Black.” The album’s powerful guitar riffs and driving rhythms helped make it a landmark of hard rock. It also introduced many listeners to Johnson’s voice as part of AC/DC’s sound. The Croatian duo 2CELLOS later performed the title song at concerts and covered “You Shook Me All Night Long” on their cellos.

Beat Saber is a virtual reality rhythm game that turns music into a fast-moving challenge. Wearing a VR headset, players hold two motion-tracked controllers that become glowing sabers, one red and one blue. As a song plays, matching colored blocks approach, and players must slice them in the directions shown by arrows on the blocks. They also dodge obstacles and avoid hitting bombs. Success depends on making each move at the right moment in the music, not just swinging quickly. Beat Saber belongs to the broader genre of rhythm games, which test a player’s sense of timing through actions synchronized with songs. Other rhythm games include osu!, where players click or tap targets, and Dance Dance Revolution, where players step on arrows to the beat.

The Fairly OddParents is a Nickelodeon animated series about Timmy Turner, a boy whose busy, oblivious parents often leave him with Vicky, a teenage babysitter who treats him badly. Timmy’s secret fairy godparents, Cosmo and Wanda, disguise themselves as his pet goldfish when other people are around. They grant his wishes to help him deal with Vicky and other problems, although those wishes often cause unexpected trouble. Vicky’s younger sister, Tootie, has a crush on Timmy. The show began as a series of shorts on Nickelodeon’s animation showcase Oh Yeah! Cartoons before becoming a full-length television series.

Through the Wire is Kanye West’s debut single, released in 2003. He recorded it after a near-fatal car crash in 2002 left his jaw broken and wired shut while it healed. You can hear how the injury affects his rapping, and the title refers to his words coming “through the wire” holding his jaw in place. The song tells the story of the crash and his recovery, showing his determination to keep making music. Its chorus uses a sped-up sample of Chaka Khan singing Through the Fire, a 1984 song from her album I Feel for You. West changed “fire” to “wire” for his title, connecting the sample to his own experience.

Camila Cabello is a Cuban-American singer-songwriter who was born in Cuba and grew up in the United States. She first became widely known as a member of Fifth Harmony, a girl group formed on The X Factor USA. The group’s other members were Ally Brooke, Normani, Dinah Jane, and Lauren Jauregui. After leaving Fifth Harmony, Cabello built a solo career with hits such as “Havana,” inspired by the Cuban city, and “Don’t Go Yet,” from her 2022 album Familia. She also recorded “Señorita,” a duet with Shawn Mendes; its title is a Spanish word, reflecting a language Cabello uses in several songs. Her music often blends pop with Latin influences.

Iron Chef is a cooking-competition television franchise that began in Japan. Its original series is set in the fictional Kitchen Stadium, where visiting chefs challenge resident champions known as Iron Chefs. Each theatrical battle reveals a featured ingredient that both chefs must use to create dishes for a panel of judges. The show’s fictional backstory presents Kitchen Stadium as the creation of a wealthy gourmand who wants to discover extraordinary cooking. In the Japanese original, actor Takeshi Kaga portrayed this flamboyant chairman. Wearing ornate costumes and speaking with dramatic flair, he announced the featured ingredient and launched each battle. The format later inspired versions such as Iron Chef America and The Next Iron Chef, but Kitchen Stadium, the ingredient reveal, and Kaga’s performance are closely associated with the original show.

Led Zeppelin was a British rock band that became one of the most influential groups of the 1970s. Its members were singer Robert Plant, guitarist Jimmy Page, bassist and keyboardist John Paul Jones, and drummer John Bonham. In “Immigrant Song,” Plant sings about coming from “the land of the ice and snow” and invokes Valhalla, a hall in Norse mythology. “Stairway to Heaven” begins gently with acoustic instruments, then builds to an electric section with a long guitar solo; its opening describes a lady who believes “all that glitters is gold.” The band also recorded “Whole Lotta Love,” built around a powerful guitar riff. Page shaped that song’s arrangement, played his electric guitar with a cello bow during its breakdown, and produced Led Zeppelin’s studio albums.

Azula is a major villain in the animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender, which aired on Nickelodeon. She is the daughter of Fire Lord Ozai, the younger sister of Zuko, and a princess of the Fire Nation. A prodigious firebender, she can produce blue flames and uses her intelligence and intimidation to gain power. Her most important victory comes in Ba Sing Se, the walled capital of the Earth Kingdom. There, Azula persuades the Dai Li, the city’s secret police, to betray the Earth King and help her take control. The fall of Ba Sing Se is a major success for the Fire Nation in its war against the other nations. Near the end of the series, Ozai names Azula Fire Lord, but her rule is brief.

Robin is the superhero identity used by several of Batman’s young crime-fighting partners in DC Comics. The original Robin was Dick Grayson, a former circus acrobat who later became the hero Nightwing and led the Teen Titans. Other characters to wear the Robin costume include Jason Todd, Tim Drake, Stephanie Brown, Carrie Kelley, and Damian Wayne. Jason Todd was killed after readers voted on his fate in the story “A Death in the Family,” but he later returned as the anti-hero Red Hood. Stephanie Brown had previously fought crime as the Spoiler, while Carrie Kelley became Robin in Frank Miller’s story The Dark Knight Returns. Damian Wayne, Batman’s son, is another Robin. Because different people have held the role, Robin is a mantle rather than one character’s name.

Minions are small, yellow, capsule-shaped characters in the animated Despicable Me films. They speak a playful mix of languages, get into slapstick trouble, and love serving villains. In the original Despicable Me, their boss is Gru, a supervillain who plans to steal the moon but changes after adopting three sisters: Margo, Edith, and Agnes. The 2015 prequel Minions follows three Minions named Kevin, Stuart, and Bob as they travel the world looking for a supervillain to serve. Their journey eventually brings them to a young Gru, showing how they met their future boss. The characters also appear in Minions: The Rise of Gru.

Bob Dylan is an American singer-songwriter whose lyrics helped make popular music a powerful way to tell stories and comment on society. Born Robert Zimmerman, he became famous during the 1960s folk revival with songs such as “The Times They Are A-Changin’,” which became associated with protest and social change. He later brought electric rock sounds into his music. His 1965 album Highway 61 Revisited, named for a major U.S. highway, includes “Like a Rolling Stone” and “Desolation Row.” Another well-known song, “Hurricane,” released in 1975, tells the story of boxer Rubin “Hurricane” Carter. In 2016, the Swedish Academy awarded Dylan the Nobel Prize in Literature for creating “new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition.”

Avatar is a 2009 science-fiction film directed by James Cameron. It takes place on Pandora, a lush moon inhabited by the Na’vi, a tall, blue-skinned people. Humans have arrived to mine a rare superconducting mineral called unobtanium, which could help address an energy shortage on Earth. To explore Pandora and interact with the Na’vi, scientists create genetically engineered bodies that combine human and Na’vi traits. These bodies, called avatars, are remotely controlled by human operators. The story follows Jake Sully, a former Marine who operates an avatar and becomes close to the Na’vi. As he learns about their lives and their connection to Pandora, he faces a choice between helping the human mining operation and protecting the people whose home it threatens.

Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth is a Batman graphic novel written by Grant Morrison and illustrated by Dave McKean. It follows Batman as he enters Arkham Asylum, Gotham City’s institution for many of his most dangerous enemies, after its inmates take control. The story combines Batman’s confrontation with the Joker and other villains with the history of the asylum and its founder. Its title echoes a line from Philip Larkin’s poem “Church Going.” McKean’s layered, painterly artwork mixes images and textures to make the building and its inhabitants feel disturbing and unpredictable. Arkham is also a recurring location in Batman stories: Dr. Jonathan Crane, the Scarecrow, has worked there, and psychiatrist Harleen Quinzel became Harley Quinn after falling for the Joker, one of its inmates.

Buzz Lightyear is a space-ranger action figure in Pixar’s Toy Story films. When he arrives in Andy’s bedroom, Buzz believes he is a real interstellar hero on a mission, not a toy. His arrival upsets Woody, a cowboy doll who had been Andy’s favorite plaything, and the two become rivals. After Buzz learns the truth about himself, he and Woody become loyal friends. Buzz first appeared in Toy Story, released in 1995 as Pixar’s first feature-length film. Later films continue their adventures alongside other toys, including Jessie the Cowgirl, who is introduced in Toy Story 2. Buzz’s name also appears in the title of the 2022 film Lightyear, which tells a different kind of space-adventure story.

The Bear is a television drama and comedy about Carmen “Carmy” Berzatto, a classically trained chef who returns to Chicago after his brother’s death. Carmy takes over his family’s struggling Italian beef sandwich shop and tries to keep it running while dealing with grief, money problems, and the intense pace of restaurant work. The series follows the kitchen staff as they argue, support one another, and learn to work as a team. Its fast-moving scenes show how stressful it can be to prepare food for customers while managing complicated personal relationships. The Bear premiered in 2022 and airs on FX and streams on Hulu. Carmy is played by Jeremy Allen White, who also played Lip Gallagher on the television series Shameless.

Released in 1937, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was Walt Disney Productions’ first full-length animated film. Based on a fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm, it follows a princess whose jealous stepmother, the Queen, orders her killed. Snow White escapes into the forest and finds shelter in a cottage belonging to seven miners, each with a distinctive personality and name, such as Grumpy, Happy, and Sleepy. The Queen later disguises herself and tricks Snow White into eating a poisoned apple. Making a feature-length cartoon was an expensive gamble at a time when audiences were used to animated shorts, but the film became a major success. Walt Disney led the studio behind it; earlier, he and animator Ub Iwerks had helped create Mickey Mouse.

Thanos is a powerful Marvel supervillain from the moon Titan and a central figure in the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s Infinity Saga. He believes the universe has too few resources to support all its living beings, so he plans to eliminate half of all life to “restore balance.” To do this, he hunts six colorful cosmic artifacts called the Infinity Stones. Each controls a different aspect of existence: space, time, reality, power, mind, or soul. The green Time Stone is kept in the Eye of Agamotto, used by Doctor Strange. The Soul Stone can be obtained only through a terrible sacrifice on Vormir, where the Red Skull acts as its guardian. After gathering all six Stones in a gauntlet, Thanos wipes out half of all life with a snap of his fingers.

Mary Poppins is a 1964 Disney musical film about Jane and Michael Banks, two children living in London whose lives change when a magical nanny named Mary Poppins arrives to care for them. She turns ordinary tasks into adventures: while the children clean their room, she sings “A Spoonful of Sugar,” explaining that finding “an element of fun” can make a job easier. Mary also sings the gentle “Feed the Birds,” which encourages kindness toward others. The children befriend Bert, a cheerful Cockney chimney sweep who sings “Chim Chim Cher-ee” and joins them in the energetic rooftop dance number “Step in Time.” Through its songs and magical adventures, the film shows how Mary helps the Banks family find more joy and closeness in everyday life.

The Good Doctor is an American medical drama created by David Shore. It follows Shaun Murphy, an autistic surgical resident with savant syndrome, as he joins the staff of San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital. Shaun has an exceptional ability to notice medical details, but he also faces challenges communicating with some patients and colleagues. The series explores his work in surgery, his relationships, and the difficult decisions doctors make while caring for patients. In the pilot episode, Shaun saves a young boy injured by falling glass at an airport, demonstrating his medical skills before he begins working at the hospital. Shaun is played by English actor Freddie Highmore, who also portrayed Norman Bates in the television series Bates Motel.

Loki is a Marvel character inspired by the trickster god of Norse mythology. In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Tom Hiddleston plays him as an Asgardian prince whose magic, shapeshifting, and schemes often bring him into conflict with his brother Thor. Loki is killed by Thanos in Avengers: Infinity War, but a version of him from an earlier point in time becomes the main character of the television series Loki. There, he is captured by the Time Variance Authority, or TVA, an organization that monitors a supposedly approved history and arrests people whose actions create unauthorized branching timelines. Its retro-futurist offices and field agents, including Mobius M. Mobius and Hunter B-15, introduce Loki to other versions of himself, known as variants, including Sylvie.

Among Us is a multiplayer social-deduction game developed by Innersloth that became a major online sensation. Players take on secret roles as crewmates or impostors. Crewmates move around a map completing tasks and trying to identify the impostors, while impostors pretend to help, sabotage the ship, and eliminate crewmates. Players can report a body or call an emergency meeting to discuss who seems suspicious. They then vote, and the chosen player may be ejected into space. Impostors can also travel through vents; an Engineer role lets crewmates use vents too. The game’s original spaceship map is called The Skeld. It includes rooms such as Cafeteria, Admin, and Electrical, and came before later maps including MIRA HQ, Polus, and the Airship.

Arnold Schwarzenegger was born in Austria and first became famous as a bodybuilder. He won the Mr. Olympia title seven times, and the documentary Pumping Iron helped introduce him to a wider audience. He later became a major action-film star, known for his muscular build and memorable roles. In the 1984 science-fiction action film The Terminator, Schwarzenegger plays a cyborg sent from the future to kill Sarah Connor. Another time traveler, Kyle Reese, goes back to protect her. The film became one of Schwarzenegger’s best-known movies. After his acting career made him a household name, he entered politics and served as governor of California from 2003 to 2011.

Jojo Rabbit is a 2019 satirical coming-of-age film set in Nazi Germany during World War II. Its main character, Jojo Betzler, is a young boy in the Jungvolk, a Nazi youth group, who has an imaginary friend: a foolish, comic version of Adolf Hitler. Jojo’s beliefs are challenged when he discovers that his mother is hiding a Jewish girl in their home. His friend Yorki is also a member of the Jungvolk. The film uses humor alongside serious events to show how propaganda can shape a child’s thinking and how empathy can change it. New Zealand filmmaker Taika Waititi directed the film and played Jojo’s imaginary Hitler. He won an Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay for Jojo Rabbit, which ends with a line from a poem by Rainer Maria Rilke.

Daniel Kaluuya is a British actor known for playing Chris Washington in Get Out and OJ Haywood in Nope. Both films were written and directed by Jordan Peele, and both use horror and suspense to explore larger themes. In the 2021 biographical drama Judas and the Black Messiah, directed by Shaka King, Kaluuya portrayed Fred Hampton, a leader of the Illinois chapter of the Black Panther Party. The film follows the FBI’s infiltration of the chapter through informant Bill O’Neal, played by LaKeith Stanfield. Kaluuya’s performance as Hampton earned him the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

Captain Jack Sparrow is a fictional pirate portrayed by Johnny Depp in Disney’s Pirates of the Caribbean film franchise. He is famous for his distinctive swagger, eccentric manner, clever tricks, and ability to escape danger through quick thinking as much as sword fighting. The series began in 2003 with Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl, an adventure film inspired by a Disney theme-park attraction. In that first movie, Jack pursues the Black Pearl, a ship taken from him by Captain Barbossa, played by Geoffrey Rush. Barbossa and his crew are under a curse that makes them appear as skeletons in moonlight. Jack’s unpredictable behavior often hides his skill as a pirate, making him one of the franchise’s central characters.

Bugsnax is an adventure game set on Snaktooth Island, where a journalist arrives to investigate the disappearance of explorer Elizabert Megafig. The island is home to the Bugsnax: living creatures that combine animal traits with foods. Some look like walking strawberries or other snacks, and the player catches them using traps and other tools. As the journalist explores, they interview the island’s residents, learn more about the unusual creatures, and search for clues about what happened to Elizabert. The game mixes creature-catching puzzles with a mystery story. To remember the two key facts, connect the game’s title, Bugsnax, with its bug-like food creatures, and remember that the investigation takes place on Snaktooth Island.

Isekai is a Japanese storytelling genre whose name means “another world.” In isekai anime, manga, and light novels, a character from ordinary life is transported, summoned, or reincarnated into a separate world, often one with magic, monsters, or rules like those of a video game. The story usually follows the character as they learn how this new world works and face its challenges. One example is Re:Zero, in which Subaru is sent to a fantasy world and discovers an ability called Return by Death. Whenever he dies, he returns to an earlier point in events while keeping his memories of what happened. That knowledge lets him try to change the outcome, though he must endure the experience of dying to use it.

The Brotherhood of Steel is a paramilitary order in Fallout, a video game series set after a devastating nuclear war. It was founded by Captain Roger Maxson after he uncovered unethical experiments at the Mariposa military base. Brotherhood members collect, preserve, and often restrict access to powerful technology left from before the war, believing it could be dangerous in the wrong hands. They are known for their advanced equipment, including power armor. In the Capital Wasteland, the Brotherhood reactivates Liberty Prime, a colossal pre-war combat robot. Liberty Prime fights with a powerful laser weapon and nuclear-powered explosives, making it one of the Brotherhood’s most memorable allies.

Anime is a broad term for Japanese animation, including television series and films. It covers many genres and stories: Naruto follows a young ninja who hopes to become the leader of his village, Dragon Ball Z features martial-arts battles involving Saiyan warriors, and Demon Slayer follows siblings fighting demons in Taisho-era Japan. Anime films can tell very different kinds of stories. In the 2001 film Spirited Away, a girl named Chihiro becomes trapped in a world of spirits and must find a way to save her parents. Its director, Hayao Miyazaki, co-founded the animation studio Studio Ghibli with fellow filmmaker Isao Takahata. These examples show that anime can range from action-packed television adventures to imaginative feature films.

Leonard Cohen was a Montreal-born Canadian singer-songwriter, poet, and novelist whose songs often explored love, faith, and loss. He first released “Hallelujah” on his 1984 album Various Positions, which his record label, Columbia, initially declined to release in the United States. The song became much more widely known through later versions, including a recording by Jeff Buckley. Another Cohen song, “You Want It Darker,” appeared near the end of his life. In 2020, the Republican National Convention used “Hallelujah” despite Cohen’s estate having denied permission, prompting the estate to object publicly. A spokesperson even said the estate might have considered a request to use “You Want It Darker” instead.

21 Savage is the stage name of Shéyaa Bin Abraham-Joseph, a British-American rapper who grew up in Atlanta. His solo hit “Bank Account” helped bring him a wider audience, and his calm delivery over dark beats became a recognizable part of his sound. He has also worked with Drake, appearing alongside Project Pat on “Knife Talk” from Certified Lover Boy and on “Jimmy Cooks” from Honestly, Nevermind. Another important collaborator is Atlanta producer Metro Boomin. The two shared billing on the 2016 EP Savage Mode, whose spare, eerie production helped define 21 Savage’s early style. They reunited for Savage Mode II in 2020, continuing a partnership that has been central to his music.

Pokémon is a Nintendo-originated multimedia franchise that began with role-playing video games released in Japan in 1996. Players explore different regions, collect creatures called Pokémon, train them, and battle other trainers. The franchise grew to include an anime series, trading cards, films, and many more games. Pikachu and Charizard are two of its best-known Pokémon. Each main game is set in a region with its own towns, characters, and creatures. Pokémon Diamond and Pearl take place in Sinnoh, a region inspired by Japan’s northern island of Hokkaido. Sinnoh’s legendary Pokémon include Dialga and Palkia. Pokémon Legends: Arceus explores an older version of Sinnoh called Hisui.

Chadwick Boseman, the actor best known for playing T’Challa, the superhero king in Black Panther, died on August 28, 2020, at age 43. His family announced that he had been diagnosed with stage III colon cancer in 2016 and had privately battled the illness for four years as it advanced to stage IV. Colon cancer affects the colon, which is part of the large intestine. Boseman continued acting during his treatment, and the public did not know about his diagnosis before his death. The announcement of Chadwick Boseman’s death became the most-liked tweet in history at the time. To honor him, ABC aired Black Panther without commercials and produced a retrospective called A Tribute for a King.

The Joker is one of Batman’s most famous enemies in DC Comics: a dangerous criminal with clown makeup, a chilling grin, and a taste for chaos. His real identity and past change across different stories. In Alan Moore and Brian Bolland’s graphic novel The Killing Joke, one possible origin portrays him as a failed comedian who falls into a vat of chemicals. Batman often sends the Joker to Arkham Asylum, a Gotham City institution for criminals with serious mental illnesses that holds many of Batman’s enemies. Harleen Quinzel worked there as a doctor before the Joker drew her into his criminal world as Harley Quinn. Arkham Asylum is also the subject of a graphic novel by Grant Morrison and Dave McKean, subtitled A Serious House on Serious Earth.

Don McLean is an American singer-songwriter best known for two songs released in 1971: “American Pie” and “Vincent.” “American Pie” is a long, story-like song that looks back on the early rock-and-roll era and uses images of change and loss. Its phrase “the day the music died” refers to a 1959 plane crash that killed musicians Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and the Big Bopper. That phrase became a common nickname for the tragedy. “Vincent” is a quieter ballad addressed to the Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh; it begins by evoking his painting The Starry Night and reflects on his art and struggles. Together, the songs show how McLean used music to tell stories about people and cultural history.

“MONTERO (Call Me by Your Name)” is a 2021 single by Lil Nas X, the hip-hop artist who also made “Old Town Road.” Its music video begins in a surreal garden and uses fantasy and religious imagery to tell a provocative story. After being judged, Lil Nas X descends a pole into an underworld resembling Hell. There, he gives a lap dance to its horned ruler, Satan, before killing him and taking his place. These scenes sparked debate, but Lil Nas X has described the song and video as a way to express his identity and challenge shame directed at LGBTQ people. The song’s full title includes both “MONTERO,” a reference to the artist’s first name, and the phrase “Call Me by Your Name.”

The Strokes are a New York City rock band known for their sharp guitar riffs, catchy melodies, and stripped-down sound. Their 2001 debut album, Is This It, helped spark a revival of indie and garage rock and was later named the best album of the 2000s by the British music magazine NME. The band’s 2020 album, The New Abnormal, includes the songs “Brooklyn Bridge to Chorus” and “Ode to the Mets.” Lead singer Julian Casablancas has also worked with artists outside the band. He sang on “Instant Crush,” a track from the 2013 album Random Access Memories by the French electronic duo Daft Punk. Daft Punk’s other well-known songs include “One More Time” and “Get Lucky.”

Ana de Armas is a Cuban-Spanish actress known for playing characters in mysteries, science fiction, and action films. In the 2019 film Knives Out, she plays Marta Cabrera, a compassionate nurse who cared for wealthy mystery novelist Harlan Thrombey. Marta’s unusual inability to lie without vomiting becomes an important clue as investigators examine his death. De Armas also plays Joi, a holographic companion, in Blade Runner 2049, and Paloma, a CIA agent who helps James Bond, in No Time to Die. In the 2022 film Blonde, she portrays Marilyn Monroe. These roles show her range, but the key connection to remember is that Ana de Armas is the actress, while Marta Cabrera is the nurse she plays in Knives Out.

Death Note is a 2017 American supernatural thriller directed by Adam Wingard. It adapts a Japanese manga and anime series about a notebook that can kill a person when their name is written in it. The film moves the story to Seattle, where high-school student Light Turner discovers the notebook and begins using its power. As Light tries to decide who deserves to die, his actions draw the attention of investigators and put people close to him in danger. Netflix took over the film after acquiring its rights from Warner Bros. and released it through its streaming service. Netflix is also known for House of Cards, its first original television series.

Elon Musk is a technology entrepreneur born in South Africa. He founded SpaceX, a company that builds rockets and spacecraft, and is the CEO of Tesla, which makes electric cars. Musk is also known for his posts on social media, which have sometimes affected Tesla’s stock price. In 2020, for example, Tesla shares fell after he tweeted that he thought the company’s stock price was “too high.” In 2022, Musk bought the social-media platform Twitter for about $44 billion, following months of disputes over the deal. After the purchase, he renamed the platform X. So if a question asks who founded SpaceX, leads Tesla, and bought Twitter, the answer is Elon Musk; if it asks for Twitter’s new name, the answer is X.

FiveThirtyEight is a data-driven news website founded by statistician Nate Silver during the 2008 U.S. election cycle. Its name refers to the 538 votes in the Electoral College, which decides presidential elections. The site became known for combining results from many opinion polls with statistical models to forecast elections, rather than relying on a single poll. Polls ask a sample of people what they think or how they plan to vote, but their results can be misleading if some groups are missed or people do not answer honestly. FiveThirtyEight later expanded beyond elections to cover sports, politics, and other subjects through data journalism. Before founding the site, Silver gained prominence in baseball analytics by creating PECOTA, a system that projects how players might perform.

Scott Conant is an American chef and television personality best known to many viewers as a judge on the Food Network competition Chopped. On Chopped, chefs open baskets of mystery ingredients and must turn them into dishes for the judges to taste. Conant is especially memorable for his strong dislike of raw onions, which he has often mentioned while judging. He also hosted Chopped Sweets, a dessert-focused spin-off of the same competition. Instead of making a range of savory and sweet courses, contestants on Chopped Sweets use surprise ingredients to create desserts. If a quiz asks for the Chopped judge who dislikes raw onions and hosted the dessert spin-off, the answer is Scott Conant. If it asks for the name of that spin-off, the answer is Chopped Sweets.

A Tribe Called Quest was an influential American hip-hop group whose members were Q-Tip, Phife Dawg, Ali Shaheed Muhammad, and Jarobi White. The group became known for combining thoughtful, conversational rapping with rhythms and samples drawn from jazz. Its 1991 album The Low End Theory helped define that sound, using music by jazz artists such as Eric Dolphy and Art Blakey. On the album’s track “Verses from the Abstract,” acclaimed jazz double bassist Ron Carter played on the recording. Carter had also been a member of Miles Davis’s Second Great Quintet, so his appearance created a direct link between the group’s hip-hop and the jazz tradition that inspired it.

The X-Men are a Marvel Comics superhero team founded by Professor Charles Xavier, a powerful telepath who believes mutants and humans can live together peacefully. Mutants are people born with unusual abilities, and the X-Men use their powers to protect others, even when the world fears or mistrusts them. Xavier trains young mutants at his school, which also serves as a home and base for the team. One of the X-Men’s longtime field leaders is Scott Summers, better known as Cyclops. He fires powerful energy blasts from his eyes and wears a ruby-quartz visor to control them. Other well-known members include Storm, Wolverine, and Jean Grey. Their stories often explore prejudice, belonging, and the choice to help people despite being treated unfairly.

Charlie Puth is an American singer-songwriter, pianist, and record producer known for catchy pop songs and a talent for arranging vocals. He gained worldwide attention in 2015 when he sang and played piano on Wiz Khalifa’s “See You Again,” a song from the Furious 7 soundtrack that honors actor Paul Walker. Puth later released his debut album, Nine Track Mind, and scored a solo hit with “Attention,” a song about someone who seems to want attention rather than a relationship. “Attention” and another hit, “How Long,” appear on his second studio album, Voicenotes, released in 2018. Puth often uses layered harmonies and studio effects in his recordings, drawing on both his piano skills and his interest in music production.

Elijah Wood is an American actor best known for playing Frodo Baggins in Peter Jackson’s The Lord of the Rings film trilogy, based on J.R.R. Tolkien’s fantasy novels. Frodo is a hobbit entrusted with carrying a powerful ring on a dangerous journey. In 2020, Wood drew attention for a much lighter adventure: he visited another player’s island in Animal Crossing: New Horizons to sell turnips, and fans noticed how polite he was. Animal Crossing is a Nintendo life-simulation video game series in which players create homes, interact with animal-like villagers, and trade with other players.
