New Horizons, released in March 2020, made island visits and trading a popular way for players to connect.

The Seventh Seal is a 1957 Swedish film directed by Ingmar Bergman. It follows Antonius Block, a knight played by Max von Sydow, as he returns to a land devastated by the Black Plague. Block is troubled by questions about faith, God, and the meaning of life. When a pale figure dressed in black comes for him, Block recognizes the figure as Death and challenges him to a game of chess, hoping to delay his fate. As the game continues, Block meets people whose experiences deepen his questions and give him reasons to value the time he has left. The film’s famous chess match and its final image, inspired by the medieval “dance of death,” show how people respond to the knowledge that life must end.

V for Vendetta is a 2005 film adapted from a graphic novel by writer Alan Moore and artist David Lloyd. Set in a future Britain ruled by a totalitarian government, it follows V, a masked anarchist who fights the regime and tries to inspire others to resist it. V wears a Guy Fawkes mask and is played by Hugo Weaving. He draws a young woman named Evey Hammond into the struggle, and she becomes his protégée as she learns to question the government’s power. Natalie Portman plays Evey. Portman is also known for playing Padmé Amidala in the Star Wars prequel films and Jacqueline Kennedy in the film Jackie.

Omar Sharif was an Egyptian actor who became an international star through two films directed by David Lean. His breakthrough came in Lawrence of Arabia (1962), a sweeping World War I epic famous for its desert landscapes and cinematography. Sharif played Sherif Ali, an Arab tribal leader who becomes an ally of T. E. Lawrence, the British officer portrayed by Peter O’Toole. A few years later, Sharif played the title character in Doctor Zhivago (1965), adapted from Boris Pasternak’s novel. His character is a physician and poet whose life is shaped by revolution and war in Russia. Before these international roles, Sharif had already acted in films in his native Egypt, including The Blazing Sun.

“It’s Morbin’ Time” is a viral catchphrase associated with Morbius, a 2022 superhero film starring Jared Leto. Leto plays Dr. Michael Morbius, a Marvel biochemist whose attempt to cure his rare blood disease turns him into a “living vampire.” The phrase jokes about what he might say before transforming, but he never actually says it in the movie. It parodies the Power Rangers’ famous transformation call, “It’s Morphin’ Time,” by replacing “Morphin’” with “Morbin’,” a made-up word based on Morbius’s name. As people shared jokes and clips online, the invented line became more famous than much of the film itself. To remember the distinction: “It’s Morbin’ Time” is the meme phrase, while Morbius is the film’s title character.

Creeper World is a series of strategy and tower defense games in which players protect Odin City from the Creeper, a dangerous, fluid-like substance that spreads across the map in advancing waves. Instead of fighting individual monsters, players must stop a rising flood of Creeper from reaching and overwhelming their settlement. They do this by building weapons and other structures, connecting them to a power network, and choosing where to place their defenses. The Creeper can flow through low ground and gather in deep areas, so the shape of the land matters when planning a defense. Although Minecraft also has enemies called creepers, those are green creatures that explode near players. In Creeper World, the Creeper is a spreading substance, and Odin City is the place players defend.

The Good Place is an NBC fantasy sitcom about four deceased humans who arrive in a seemingly perfect afterlife neighborhood. Eleanor Shellstrop believes she was admitted by mistake because she was not a particularly good person during her life. She asks Chidi Anagonye, a Senegalese ethics professor, to teach her moral philosophy so she can become better. Chidi understands ethical theories but is so indecisive that even everyday choices can be agonizing for him. Their neighbors include Tahani Al-Jamil, who lived in the shadow of her sister Kamilah, and Jason Mendoza, who pretends to be a monk. With help from Janet, an all-knowing being, they investigate strange events in the neighborhood. Their efforts to improve themselves become part of a larger mystery involving the Good Place and the Bad Place.

Jimmy Savile was a British radio DJ and television presenter who became one of the BBC’s most familiar faces. He presented the music programme Top of the Pops for decades and hosted Jim’ll Fix It, a BBC One show that arranged special experiences for children who wrote in with wishes. Savile died in 2011. The following year, ITV broadcast a documentary called Exposure: The Other Side of Jimmy Savile, in which people described sexual abuse by him. Many more allegations followed, revealing that his public image had concealed a long history of abuse. The Metropolitan Police began an investigation called Operation Yewtree, which later widened to examine allegations against other prominent figures. The scandal also raised serious questions about how institutions had failed to protect victims.

TikTok is a social media app built around short videos, including dances, comedy, tutorials, and clips set to music or other audio. Its For You Page is a personalized feed that recommends videos based on signals from how someone uses the app, such as what they watch, like, share, or skip. It is separate from the Following feed, which focuses on videos from accounts the user follows. Because recommendations can change as a person interacts with videos, two users may see very different For You Pages. The recommendation system is operated by ByteDance, the company that owns TikTok. ByteDance was founded in Beijing in 2012 and also operates Douyin, a related short-video app available in China.

Vincente Minnelli was an American director celebrated for colorful film musicals. He began his career designing sets and costumes for Broadway productions, then moved to the movie studio MGM, where he became known for combining music, dance, and striking visual design. He directed Gene Kelly in An American in Paris (1951) and Brigadoon (1954). Another of his best-known films is Gigi (1958), a musical adaptation of a novella by the French writer Colette. Set in Paris, it stars Leslie Caron as a young woman named Gigi and features Maurice Chevalier singing “Thank Heaven for Little Girls.” Gigi won the Academy Award for Best Picture. Minnelli was also the father of performer Liza Minnelli, who starred in the film Cabaret.

Listening to music means hearing songs or other musical recordings, whether through headphones, earbuds, or speakers. You might play a track on demand using a streaming app such as Spotify, Apple Music, Pandora, or SoundCloud, or listen to a live performance. Streaming services let people choose songs, follow artists, and discover new music. Spotify offers a playlist called Discover Weekly and a feature called Spotify Wrapped. First released in 2016 as a swipe-through year-end story, Spotify Wrapped gives each listener a personalized recap of their listening habits. It shows details such as their most-played songs and artists, total minutes spent listening, and other patterns from the year.

Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This) is a 1983 synth-pop song by the British duo Eurythmics, made up of Annie Lennox and Dave Stewart. Its prominent, repeating synthesizer riff and steady drum-machine pulse give it a cool, mechanical sound, while Lennox’s powerful lead vocal adds intensity. The lyrics include the lines “I travel the world and the seven seas” and “who am I to disagree.” The single became Eurythmics’ first number-one hit on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100. Its stark music video helped make Lennox’s striking visual style famous. She later released the solo album Diva and sang “Into the West,” an Oscar-winning song from The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King.

Frozen is a 2013 Disney animated musical set in the kingdom of Arendelle. It follows royal sisters Elsa and Anna after Elsa’s power to create ice and snow plunges the kingdom into an endless winter. Anna sets out to find Elsa and bring her home, helped by Kristoff, a mountain man who travels with his reindeer, Sven, and Olaf, a magically animated snowman. The film explores the sisters’ relationship through songs and adventure, including Elsa’s famous song “Let It Go.” Kristoff is voiced by Jonathan Groff, who also originated the role of King George III in the original Broadway cast of the musical Hamilton.

The Amazing World of Gumball is a Cartoon Network animated series about Gumball Watterson, a blue cat, and his adopted goldfish brother, Darwin. They live with the rest of the Watterson family in the fictional town of Elmore, where ordinary situations often turn into surreal adventures. One distinctive feature is its supporting cast: characters appear in many different animation styles, including 2D drawings, 3D animation and puppetry. In the episode “The Boredom,” Gumball and Darwin wander around Elmore looking for adventure. Another character, Penny, starts as a peanut with antlers and later reveals a yellow, shape-shifting fairy form. The series was created by French animator Ben Bocquelet, who developed its premise using characters he had designed for Cartoon Network Europe advertising pitches that were rejected.

Fine Line is Harry Styles’s second solo studio album, released in 2019 after his self-titled debut. Styles first became famous as a member of the boy band One Direction, then built a solo career with music that blends pop and rock. Fine Line includes the singles “Adore You” and “Watermelon Sugar.” In “Watermelon Sugar,” Styles sings about tasting strawberries on a summer evening, creating a bright, summery mood. The song became his first number-one single in the United States. Fine Line helped establish Styles as a major solo artist, and he followed it with the 2022 album Harry’s House, which includes the hit “As It Was.”

“Strawberry Fields Forever” is a 1967 Beatles song written by John Lennon and inspired by his childhood memories of Strawberry Field, a Salvation Army children’s home in Liverpool. Although its title sounds like a place full of fruit, the song is named after that home. Its dreamlike sound came from unusual studio techniques: the Beatles combined parts of two recordings made in different keys and at different tempos, changing the tape speed so they would fit together. The flute-like melody heard at the beginning is played on a Mellotron, a keyboard that produces sounds from recordings on strips of tape rather than making conventional notes. These experiments helped make the song a famous example of the Beatles’ inventive approach to recording.

Luigi is a Nintendo character known for his green clothes and for being Mario’s younger, taller brother. He often appears as the second player in Mario games, but he also has adventures of his own. In Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels, Luigi can jump higher and farther than Mario, although his movement is harder to control. He is the star of the Luigi’s Mansion series, in which he explores haunted buildings and captures ghosts. In the original Luigi’s Mansion, released in 2001, an inventor named Professor E. Gadd gives him the Poltergust 3000, a modified vacuum cleaner that can suck up ghosts. These abilities and adventures help distinguish Luigi from his red-wearing brother.

The SCP Foundation is a fictional secret organization in a collaborative horror-fiction setting. Writers on the SCP Wiki create case-file entries about strange objects, creatures, and events, describing how the Foundation studies and contains them. Its motto is “Secure, Contain, Protect.” One famous entry, SCP-173, describes a statue that can snap a person’s neck when no one is watching it. The stories also include D-class personnel, often portrayed as prisoners used in dangerous tests. SCP-582 is connected to Slenderman, a tall, thin figure from internet folklore who stalks people in the woods. In the SCP story, SCP-582 can take on properties from stories written about it. Slenderman also partly inspired creatures found in Minecraft’s End.

MasterChef Junior is an American reality television cooking competition in which young home cooks prepare dishes and take on culinary challenges. It is the children’s spin-off of MasterChef, a competition for adult home cooks. In each episode, the contestants work in a professional-style kitchen, and a panel of judges tastes their food and decides who advances. One judge on the American version is Gordon Ramsay, a British chef also known for hosting Hell’s Kitchen and Kitchen Nightmares. He has a reputation for blunt criticism, though he guides and encourages the young contestants on MasterChef Junior. Ramsay also appeared on the interview show Hot Ones, where he ate ten increasingly spicy chicken wings while answering questions.

Gumball Watterson is the blue cat at the center of Cartoon Network’s animated comedy The Amazing World of Gumball. He lives with the Watterson family in the fictional town of Elmore, where ordinary places such as school and home become settings for strange adventures. Gumball’s younger sister, Anais, is a pink rabbit, and his adopted brother and best friend, Darwin, is an orange goldfish who grew legs. The show is known for its mixed-media look: characters made with hand-drawn animation, computer-generated imagery (CGI), stop-motion, and even live action appear together. Gumball and Darwin often set out to find excitement, as they do in the episode “The Boredom,” when they wander around Elmore looking for an adventure.

Discord is a digital communication platform where people gather in online communities called servers. Each server can have separate channels for different topics, including text channels for written messages and voice channels where members can talk or share video. Discord was originally associated with gaming, but people also use it for study groups, clubs, and interests such as quizbowl. Reflecting this wider use, Discord changed its motto in 2020 from “Chat for Gamers” to “Your place to talk.” During the COVID-19 pandemic, groups also met online using Zoom, a videoconferencing service that became widely popular and could be used alongside Discord. After criticism of its digital security, Zoom paused work on non-security features for 90 days to focus on addressing those concerns.

Tupac Shakur was an American rapper and actor who became one of hip-hop’s most influential figures in the 1990s. Born Lesane Parish Crooks, he made his film debut as Bishop in the 1992 crime drama Juice. His songs explored poverty, racism, violence, and life in the United States, while his public rivalry with fellow rapper The Notorious B.I.G. drew widespread attention. Tupac’s 1996 double album All Eyez on Me includes “California Love,” featuring Dr. Dre, as well as “Ambitionz Az a Ridah” and “I Ain’t Mad at Cha.” The album’s title was also used for a 2017 biographical film about him. Tupac was killed after a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in 1996, but his music and screen performances remain widely discussed.

Al Jazeera is a Qatar-based news organization that began in 1996 as an Arabic-language satellite news channel. Headquartered in Doha, it grew into one of the largest broadcasters in the Arabic-speaking world and now reaches international audiences through television and digital reporting. Its journalists cover politics, conflicts, and other major events. One of its best-known reporters was Shireen Abu Akleh, a Palestinian-American journalist who worked for Al Jazeera Arabic for many years. She was killed in May 2022 while covering an Israeli military raid in Jenin, in the occupied West Bank. Her death drew worldwide attention to the dangers journalists face when reporting from conflict zones.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is a 2017 open-world action-adventure game in which players control Link, a warrior exploring the kingdom of Hyrule. Link wakes in the Shrine of Resurrection after sleeping for 100 years, with little memory of what happened. During that time, a disaster known as the Great Calamity devastated Hyrule, and Princess Zelda has struggled to contain its source, Calamity Ganon. Link can travel across the world in many different ways, solving puzzles, fighting enemies, and preparing to confront Ganon. An important tool is the Sheikah Slate, an ancient tablet-like device that lets Link view a map, take pictures, and use special abilities called runes. Two of these are Magnesis, which moves metal objects, and Stasis, which briefly freezes objects in place.

Singin’ in the Rain is a 1952 musical comedy set in Hollywood as movies changed from silent films to “talkies” with recorded dialogue. Gene Kelly plays silent-film star Don Lockwood, whose career is threatened when his co-star’s voice proves unsuitable for sound films. Debbie Reynolds plays Kathy Selden, an aspiring actress who helps by dubbing the co-star’s voice, while Donald O’Connor plays Don’s friend Cosmo Brown. One comic song, “Moses Supposes,” turns a diction lesson into a lively dance number built around the tongue twister “Moses supposes his toeses are roses.” The film was co-directed by Kelly and Stanley Donen, who later directed Charade and Two for the Road.

All Eyez on Me is Tupac Shakur’s fourth studio album, released in 1996. It was his first double album, meaning it contained enough music to be issued on two discs rather than one. The album includes “California Love,” a hit featuring Dr. Dre, and “2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted,” featuring Snoop Dogg. Its title reflects the intense public attention Tupac faced as one of hip-hop’s biggest stars. All Eyez on Me came out through Death Row Records, the influential label co-founded by Suge Knight and Dr. Dre. Death Row also released Dr. Dre’s The Chronic and Snoop Dogg’s Doggystyle, helping bring West Coast rap to a huge audience. A 2017 biographical film about Tupac shares the album’s title.

Dogmeat is the name used for canine companions in several Fallout video games. Fallout takes place after a nuclear war, when survivors emerge from protective vaults into a dangerous wasteland. In Fallout 4, Dogmeat is a loyal German shepherd the player can recruit soon after reaching the Commonwealth, the game’s region around Boston. He can follow scents, find hidden items, and help fight enemies. Players first meet him beside an abandoned service station on the road from Sanctuary Hills toward Concord. That location’s full in-game name is Red Rocket Truck Stop. Although dogs named Dogmeat appear in earlier Fallout games, this German shepherd is the companion players encounter in Fallout 4.

The Last Duel is a 2021 historical drama directed by Ridley Scott and set in medieval France. It follows a dispute between knight Jean de Carrouges, played by Matt Damon, and Jacques Le Gris, played by Adam Driver. Jean’s wife, Marguerite de Carrouges, portrayed by Jodie Comer, accuses Le Gris of raping her. When Le Gris denies the charge, Jean demands a trial by combat: a judicial duel in which people believed God would allow the truthful side to win. The film presents the events from the different perspectives of Jean, Le Gris, and Marguerite, showing how their accounts conflict. Its title refers to the duel between the two men, considered the final officially sanctioned trial by combat in French history.

Jimmy Wales is an American internet entrepreneur best known for co-founding Wikipedia with Larry Sanger in 2001. Wikipedia is a free online encyclopedia that volunteers around the world can write and edit. It became one of the most visited nonprofit websites, offering articles on topics from science and history to popular culture. Because many people can contribute, its articles can improve quickly, but they can also contain mistakes or reflect bias. Wikipedia’s Women in Red project works to reduce a gender gap by encouraging more biographies of notable women. Wales also launched Wikia in 2004, a platform for fan-created wikis about fictional worlds and other interests. Wikia is now called Fandom.

At the 94th Academy Awards in March 2022, comedian Chris Rock joked that Jada Pinkett Smith could star in “G.I. Jane 2,” referring to her closely shaved hair. Pinkett Smith had spoken publicly about alopecia, a condition that causes hair loss. Her husband, actor Will Smith, walked onto the stage and slapped Rock, then returned to his seat. The moment became known as the Will Smith–Chris Rock Oscars incident and sparked widespread discussion about the joke and Smith’s response. Later that evening, Smith won Best Actor for playing Richard Williams in King Richard and apologized during his acceptance speech. The ceremony took place at the Dolby Theatre in the Hollywood & Highland complex. Previously named the Kodak Theatre after the photography company, it hosted the Oscars from 2002 to 2019 and again in 2022.

Titanic is a 1997 romantic historical disaster film directed by James Cameron. Set aboard the British luxury liner RMS Titanic during its ill-fated maiden voyage in 1912, it follows Jack Dawson, a young passenger played by Leonardo DiCaprio, and Rose DeWitt Bukater, a first-class passenger played by British actress Kate Winslet. Jack and Rose fall in love despite their different social backgrounds, but their story is interrupted when the ship strikes an iceberg and sinks. Jack later dies of hypothermia in the freezing water. The film combines their fictional romance with the real Titanic disaster and includes a present-day search for a valuable diamond called the Heart of the Ocean. Winslet also appeared in Sense and Sensibility and The Reader.

Lover is a 2019 studio album by American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift. It followed her 2017 album Reputation and came before folklore and evermore, two albums she released in 2020. Lover includes the upbeat single “Me!,” the pop song “You Need to Calm Down,” and “Miss Americana & the Heartbreak Prince.” That last song helped inspire the title of the 2020 documentary Taylor Swift: Miss Americana, which follows Swift as she becomes more willing to speak publicly about her beliefs and experiences. In 2021, Swift also directed a short film to accompany the 10-minute version of her song “All Too Well.” If a question asks which album contains those three songs, the answer is Lover; if it asks who made the album, the answer is Taylor Swift.

Moneyball is a 2011 sports drama starring Brad Pitt as Billy Beane, the real-life general manager of the Oakland Athletics, also known as the Oakland A’s. The film is based on Michael Lewis’s book about how Beane tried to build a competitive baseball team despite having far less money to spend than many rival clubs. Working with an assistant, he used statistical analysis to identify players whose skills were valuable but often overlooked by traditional scouts. This approach is associated with sabermetrics, the study of baseball performance through detailed statistics. Rather than simply choosing famous or expensive players, Beane looked for affordable players who could help the team win. Moneyball dramatizes the resistance he faced as well as the A’s effort to succeed with an unconventional roster.

The New Yorker is an American magazine founded in 1925. It is known for combining in-depth journalism and criticism with cartoons, essays, and short fiction. Although its name refers to New York City, it covers stories and ideas from around the world. In 1946, the magazine devoted an entire issue to John Hersey’s Hiroshima, a report on the atomic bombing of the Japanese city and its effects on survivors. The New Yorker also published fiction by South African author Nadine Gordimer for more than five decades. Gordimer wrote July’s People, a novel about the Smales family during imagined political upheaval in South Africa. After Nelson Mandela died, she was chosen to write a eulogy for him in the magazine.

A rhythm game is a video game that challenges players to perform actions in time with music. As a song plays, visual cues such as scrolling notes or arrows show when to press a button, tap a screen, swing a controller, or move their feet. Good timing helps players score points and keep a streak of successful moves. In Guitar Hero, players press controls to match notes from a song. In Beat Saber, they slice colored blocks in virtual reality, while osu! includes challenges such as clicking circles. One of the best-known rhythm games is Konami’s arcade series Dance Dance Revolution, first released in 1998. Players stand on a dance platform and step on its directional panels as matching arrows scroll upward on a screen.

Prometheus is a 2012 science-fiction film directed by Ridley Scott and developed as a prequel to the Alien franchise. Archaeologists Elizabeth Shaw and Charlie Holloway discover matching star maps in ancient cultures and interpret them as an invitation from the beings who created humanity. They join a mission aboard the spaceship Prometheus to the distant moon LV-223, hoping to meet those creators, known as the Engineers. The crew also includes David, a synthetic human played by Michael Fassbender. While the human passengers spend the long voyage in cryosleep, David remains awake. He watches the classic film Lawrence of Arabia and practices the speech and mannerisms of its star, Peter O’Toole. Once the crew reaches LV-223, their search for answers leads to dangerous discoveries about the Engineers and the origins of the Alien series.

The Greatest Showman is a 2017 musical film inspired by the life of P. T. Barnum, played by Hugh Jackman. It follows Barnum as he brings together performers with unusual talents to build a spectacular show. Zac Efron plays Phillip Carlyle, a playwright who joins the production, while Zendaya plays Anne Wheeler, a skilled trapeze artist who performs with her brother. Anne and Phillip fall in love, but their relationship faces prejudice because they come from different social backgrounds. Their feelings are explored in the duet “Rewrite the Stars.” Another well-known song from the film, “A Million Dreams,” expresses Barnum’s hopes for the future. Through its music and performances, the film tells a story about ambition, belonging, and the desire to be accepted.

AJR is an American pop trio made up of brothers Adam, Jack, and Ryan Met. Their initials form the band’s name. The brothers are known for catchy songs that mix pop music with unusual sounds and personal lyrics. Their best-known tracks include “Weak,” “Bang!,” and “Sober Up.” AJR’s 2017 album The Click also includes “Netflix Trip,” a song inspired by the sitcom The Office. Rather than simply retelling the show, it uses moments involving its characters to reflect on growing up and the memories people connect to their favorite stories. This makes “Netflix Trip” an example of how AJR can turn a familiar piece of entertainment into a song about personal experiences.

“The Girl from Ipanema,” originally titled “Garota de Ipanema,” is a Brazilian bossa nova song composed by Antônio Carlos Jobim, with Portuguese lyrics by Vinícius de Moraes. Its gentle rhythm and melody helped bring bossa nova—a style that grew from samba in Rio de Janeiro—to audiences around the world. The song describes a beautiful young woman walking through the Ipanema neighborhood, unaware that the singer admires her. A famous recording appears on the landmark 1964 album Getz/Gilberto, which paired American saxophonist Stan Getz with Brazilian guitarist and singer João Gilberto. João sang the Portuguese verse, while his wife at the time, Astrud Gilberto, sang the English-language part. The recording helped make “The Girl from Ipanema” a widely performed jazz-pop standard.

Iman Vellani is a Pakistani-Canadian actress who made her screen acting debut as Kamala Khan in Ms. Marvel, a six-episode series that premiered on Disney+ in summer 2022. Kamala is a superhero fan and teenager from Jersey City who discovers she has powers after putting on a mysterious golden bangle. The series follows her as she learns to use those powers while balancing family, friendships, and her new identity as Ms. Marvel. Vellani returned to the role in the 2023 Marvel Cinematic Universe film The Marvels. In that movie, Kamala’s powers become entangled with those of Carol Danvers, also known as Captain Marvel, and Monica Rambeau, bringing the three characters together.

Ted Turner is an American media entrepreneur who changed television news by founding CNN, the Cable News Network. CNN began broadcasting on June 1, 1980, as the first 24-hour cable news channel. Before then, viewers generally had to wait for scheduled news programs to learn about major events on television. CNN could report breaking stories at any hour, helping make round-the-clock news a familiar part of modern media. Turner also built a broader entertainment business: he later owned the Atlanta Braves baseball team and World Championship Wrestling, often called WCW. His best-known achievement, however, is launching CNN and showing that a television channel devoted entirely to news could reach audiences around the world.

“Alright” is a song by Kendrick Lamar and the seventh track on his 2015 album To Pimp a Butterfly. The album also includes “King Kunta,” “The Blacker the Berry,” and “How Much a Dollar Cost.” “Alright” pairs an upbeat, funk-influenced sound with a repeated message of resilience: “We gon’ be alright.” Its lyrics also address racism and police violence, including a line about police that drew controversy. Protesters adopted the refrain as a chant during Black Lives Matter demonstrations, making the song closely associated with the movement and the fight for racial justice. Lamar later performed “Alright” at the 2022 Super Bowl halftime show.

Pixar Animation Studios is an American film studio known for computer-animated movies. It grew out of the computer graphics group at Lucasfilm, the company behind Star Wars. In 1986, Pixar became independent with Apple co-founder Steve Jobs as its majority investor. Its first feature-length film, Toy Story (1995), was directed by John Lasseter and was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation. Lasseter later became Pixar’s chief creative officer, helping guide its films and creative direction. Pixar went on to make movies such as Finding Nemo and The Incredibles, combining technical innovation with stories about friendship, family, and adventure. At the start of many Pixar films, a small animated lamp jumps on and squishes the “I” in the studio’s name. The Walt Disney Company acquired Pixar in 2006.

Get Out is a 2017 horror film written and directed by Jordan Peele in his feature-film directing debut. It follows Chris Washington, a young Black photographer who visits the family of his white girlfriend, Rose Armitage. At first, her parents seem welcoming, but Chris notices unsettling behavior among the Black people working at their home. He discovers that the Armitage family uses hypnosis to trap victims’ minds in a powerless state called the “Sunken Place” while arranging to transplant older white people’s brains into young Black people’s bodies. The film combines suspense and horror with a critique of racism. Before making Get Out, Peele was best known as one half of the sketch-comedy duo Key & Peele, alongside Keegan-Michael Key.

Game of Thrones is an HBO fantasy television series adapted from George R. R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire novels. It follows noble families competing for the Iron Throne and control of Westeros, while supernatural dangers gather beyond the Wall in the north. Another major storyline follows Daenerys Targaryen, a member of a former ruling family, as she seeks to reclaim its power with the help of her dragons. In the city of Astapor, Daenerys acquires the Unsullied, an elite army of eunuch soldiers trained from childhood and known for fighting with spears. She then frees them, and many choose to follow her. One of their leaders is Grey Worm.

Spider-Man is the superhero identity of Peter Parker, a New York teenager who gains extraordinary strength, agility, and the ability to cling to walls after being bitten by a radioactive spider. Peter builds web-shooters that let him swing between buildings and catch criminals. One of his recurring opponents is Dr. Michael Morbius, a scientist with a rare blood disease. Trying to cure himself, Morbius performs an experiment that transforms him into a “living vampire” who needs blood to survive. He first appeared in The Amazing Spider-Man #101 and has fought Spider-Man several times, though he is sometimes portrayed as a tragic figure rather than a purely evil villain. Tom Holland plays Spider-Man in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, while Jared Leto played Morbius in a 2022 film.

The Weeknd is the stage name of Abel Makkonen Tesfaye, a Canadian singer-songwriter and producer known for blending R&B with pop and electronic music. He first gained attention by releasing songs online, then became a major star with hits such as “The Hills” and “Blinding Lights.” His 2022 album Dawn FM is presented like a radio broadcast, with songs that explore memory, regret, and change. The Weeknd has also worked with other artists. He collaborated with rapper Juice WRLD on “Smile,” a track released on Juice WRLD’s posthumous 2020 album Legends Never Die. If asked for the artist behind Dawn FM or those hits, the answer is The Weeknd; if asked for his song with Juice WRLD on Legends Never Die, the answer is “Smile.”

Batman Returns is a 1992 superhero film directed by Tim Burton. Set in a dark, snowy Gotham City, it follows Batman as he confronts the Penguin, a villain seeking power, and Catwoman, a mysterious figure who sometimes opposes him. The film’s unsettling scenes and violence surprised some families who expected a children’s adventure. Its graphic content contributed to the cancellation of a planned promotional tie-in with McDonald’s Happy Meal, the children’s meal that typically includes food and a toy. McDonald’s is the fast-food chain known for its Golden Arches. The controversy shows how a movie’s tone can affect marketing: even when a film features a popular comic-book hero, companies may decide it is unsuitable to promote to young children.

“Misery Business” is a high-energy single from Paramore’s 2007 album Riot!. Sung by Hayley Williams, it tells the story of a narrator who boasts that she has won a boy away from another woman. Its fast pace and loud guitars helped make it one of the band’s best-known songs. Years later, listeners noticed similarities between “Misery Business” and Olivia Rodrigo’s “good 4 u,” a single from her 2021 debut album SOUR. “Good 4 u” combines a guitar-driven pop-rock sound with sharply sarcastic lyrics about an ex who seems to have moved on easily. After the comparisons, Paramore members Hayley Williams and Josh Farro received songwriting credits on Rodrigo’s song.

The Nightmare Before Christmas is a 1993 stop-motion animated musical fantasy film directed by Henry Selick, who later directed Coraline. Tim Burton created its story and characters, but he did not direct the film. Its main character, Jack Skellington, is the Pumpkin King of Halloween Town. Tired of his familiar holiday, Jack discovers Christmas Town, a place devoted to a winter celebration of gifts and cheer, and decides to take over Christmas himself. His well-meant plan soon causes trouble because he does not fully understand the holiday. The film uses stop-motion animation: filmmakers move figures a tiny amount between photographs, then play the images in sequence to make the characters appear to move. Its songs, spooky designs, and mix of Halloween and Christmas have made it a well-known holiday film.

Sheck Wes is the stage name of Khadimou Rassoul Cheikh Fall, an American rapper raised in Harlem, New York. He broke through with his 2017 single “Mo Bamba,” which later appeared on his debut album, Mudboy. The song’s shouted refrain helped it spread online and become a popular anthem at sports arenas. Its title comes from Mohamed “Mo” Bamba, a professional basketball player and friend of Sheck Wes who was selected sixth overall in the 2018 NBA draft and played for the Orlando Magic. Knowing that Sheck Wes is the rapper and “Mo Bamba” is the song connects the two key facts: the hit made him widely known, and its name honors an NBA center rather than describing the rapper himself.

The Incredibles is a 2004 Pixar animated film about the Parr family, whose members have different superpowers. After lawsuits force superheroes into retirement, Bob Parr, once known as Mr. Incredible, and his wife Helen, or Elastigirl, try to live ordinary lives with their children Violet, Dash, and Jack-Jack. Bob is lured to a remote island, where he encounters a powerful robot created by Syndrome, a former fan who became a villain after Bob told him to “go home.” The family reunites to stop Syndrome and his robot from attacking their city, with help from Bob’s friend Frozone. Their superhero suits are designed by the sharp-tongued Edna Mode, who refuses to add capes because she knows how easily they can catch on things and cause deadly accidents.

Squid Game is a South Korean Netflix survival drama about people in serious financial trouble who accept an invitation to compete for a life-changing cash prize. A masked organization runs the contest, turning familiar children’s activities into deadly challenges. One early game, “Red Light, Green Light,” features a giant singing doll that detects movement; a Pakistani immigrant contestant named Ali helps save the main character during it. That main character is Seong Gi-hun, who enters as Player 456. Gi-hun grew up with another contestant, Cho Sang-woo, and ultimately wins the games. The series takes its title from a Korean children’s game, contrasting the innocence of childhood play with the danger and desperation of the competition.

Eminem, whose real name is Marshall Mathers, is an American rapper and actor. Born in St. Joseph, Missouri, he grew up in the Detroit area, where he developed his rapping skills. In the 2002 film 8 Mile, he played Jimmy Smith Jr., an aspiring rapper nicknamed Rabbit who tries to succeed in Detroit’s hip-hop scene. Eminem recorded the song “Lose Yourself” for the film’s soundtrack. Its lyrics focus on overcoming fear and making the most of a rare opportunity, and it became the first hip-hop song to win the Academy Award for Best Original Song. Eminem later performed “Lose Yourself” at the 2022 Super Bowl halftime show.

HBO, short for Home Box Office, is an American subscription television network that launched in 1972. It became the first U.S. television network to transmit its signal by satellite, helping it reach viewers across the country. HBO is known for original series such as the historical drama Chernobyl, the fantasy series Game of Thrones, and Euphoria, in which the character Rue hears a reading of a poem by Rainer Maria Rilke. Another influential HBO series is The Sopranos, a crime drama created by David Chase. It stars James Gandolfini as Tony Soprano, a New Jersey mob boss who tries to balance his family life and criminal organization while seeking therapy from psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Melfi.

Riot Games is an American video game developer and publisher founded in 2006. It is best known for League of Legends, a free-to-play multiplayer online battle arena game released in 2009 and often shortened to LoL. In the game, players choose characters called champions and work with teammates to defeat an opposing team. Riot has built a major esports scene around League of Legends, with professional teams competing in tournaments watched by fans worldwide. The game’s characters also appear beyond matches: some belong to the fictional K-pop group K/DA or heavy metal band Pentakill, while champions including Vi and Jinx appear in the animated series Arcane, which is set in the game’s world. Riot Games later created the tactical shooter Valorant.

The Hidden Fortress is a 1958 Japanese adventure film directed by Akira Kurosawa. Its story begins with two quarrelsome, self-serving peasants who hope to find gold after a war. Instead, they become involved in a dangerous escape: Princess Yuki and her loyal general, Rokurota Makabe, must cross enemy territory without revealing who they are. The peasants’ greed and frequent arguments add comedy, but they also make the journey more risky. The skilled general keeps the unlikely group moving and protects the princess. Rokurota is played by Toshiro Mifune, an actor who appeared in many Kurosawa films. Mifune also played Kikuchiyo in Kurosawa’s Seven Samurai. The uneasy alliance between the peasants, the princess, and the general drives the action in The Hidden Fortress.

Beyoncé is an American singer, songwriter, and performer from Houston, Texas. She first became famous as a member of the group Destiny’s Child before launching a successful solo career. She is also known for visual albums, which pair music with films or videos; examples include Lemonade and Black Is King. Her 2022 album Renaissance, announced as the first part of a trilogy, celebrates dance music, drawing on styles such as house and disco. Its cover shows Beyoncé sitting atop a reflective horse. The album’s lead single, “BREAK MY SOUL,” opens with a vocal sample from Big Freedia’s song “Explode.” With its dance beat and lyrics about letting go of anger and freeing your mind, the song captures the album’s energetic spirit.

Bong Joon-ho is a South Korean filmmaker known for mixing suspense, dark humor, and social criticism. He directed and co-wrote the 2019 film Parasite, in which the struggling Kim family gradually secures jobs as a tutor, art therapist, chauffeur, and housekeeper in the wealthy Park family’s home. As the two families’ lives become entangled, the film explores the divide between rich and poor through surprising and sometimes unsettling events. Parasite won the Palme d’Or, the top prize at the Cannes Film Festival, and became the first non-English-language film to win the Academy Award for Best Picture. Bong’s other films include Memories of Murder, a crime thriller, and The Host, a monster movie.

“Break My Soul” is an upbeat dance song Beyoncé released in June 2022 as the lead single from her album Renaissance. Its energetic beat fits the album’s celebration of dance music, including disco and house, while its lyrics encourage listeners to let go of stress and find joy. The song opens with a vocal sample from “Explode,” a 2014 track by Big Freedia, a New Orleans bounce musician. In that sample, Freedia repeats the word “yaka,” giving the opening a distinctive sound. “Break My Soul” became Beyoncé’s first solo single to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 since 2008.

Pink Floyd was an English rock band formed in London in 1965. Known for experimental sounds, thoughtful lyrics and elaborate live shows, the group became one of the most influential acts in rock history. Its ambitious albums include The Dark Side of the Moon, which explores themes such as time and mortality, and The Wall, a story about isolation. Pink Floyd’s original frontman, Syd Barrett, was a major songwriter on the band’s 1967 debut album, The Piper at the Gates of Dawn. He left the group in 1968, but continued making music as a solo artist. His solo albums include The Madcap Laughs and Barrett, released in 1970; Barrett features the songs “Baby Lemonade” and “Gigolo Aunt.”

Rear Window is a 1954 mystery film directed by Alfred Hitchcock. James Stewart plays L.B. “Jeff” Jefferies, a photographer stuck in his apartment while his broken leg heals. To pass the time, he watches his neighbors through his rear window, which looks across a courtyard. When he notices strange activity in one apartment, he begins to suspect that a neighbor has murdered his wife. His girlfriend, Lisa Fremont, a fashion model played by Grace Kelly, joins him in investigating the woman’s disappearance. Much of the suspense comes from Jeff trying to piece together what happened using only what he can see from his window. The film also raises a question: when does curiosity about other people’s lives become an invasion of privacy?

Taylor Swift: Miss Americana is a 2020 documentary directed by filmmaker Lana Wilson, who also made The Departure, a film about a Japanese man who helps people disappear. Using candid footage and interviews, Miss Americana follows singer-songwriter Taylor Swift through changes in her career and personal life. It shows her questioning the pressure to maintain a “good girl” image and learning to speak more openly about her beliefs, including her political views. The film’s title echoes “Miss Americana & the Heartbreak Prince,” a song from Swift’s 2019 album Lover. Together, these details identify the documentary by its full title, Taylor Swift: Miss Americana, and its director as Lana Wilson.

The Wizard of Oz is a 1939 musical fantasy film starring Judy Garland as Dorothy, a girl from Kansas whose house is swept away by a tornado and lands in the magical land of Oz. Hoping to get home, Dorothy follows the yellow brick road to the Emerald City, where she seeks help from the Wizard. Along the way, she meets the Scarecrow, who wants a brain; the Tin Woodman, who wants a heart; and the Cowardly Lion, who wants courage. The story also inspired Wicked, a stage musical that reimagines Oz through the friendship between Glinda and Elphaba, who becomes the Witch of the West. One of Wicked’s best-known songs is “Defying Gravity,” sung by Elphaba.

Future Nostalgia is Dua Lipa’s second studio album, released in March 2020 as the follow-up to her self-titled 2017 debut. It blends modern pop with dance sounds inspired by earlier decades, giving the album a sound that feels both new and familiar. Its songs include “Levitating,” which opens with an invitation to travel through a galaxy, and “Love Again,” which describes the surprise of falling in love again. The album’s lead single, “Don’t Start Now,” came out in November 2019. With a nu-disco groove and lyrics about moving on after a breakup, it became a major hit. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, making it Dua Lipa’s highest-charting solo single in the United States at the time.

She-Hulk is a Marvel superhero whose everyday identity is Jennifer Walters, an attorney and cousin of Bruce Banner, the Hulk. After receiving a blood transfusion from Bruce, Jennifer gains gamma-powered abilities: she can transform into a green-skinned hero with enormous strength and durability. Unlike Bruce’s early Hulk transformations, Jennifer generally keeps her intelligence and personality, allowing her to work as a lawyer as well as a superhero. She-Hulk has fought alongside several Marvel teams, including A-Force, an all-female offshoot of the Avengers introduced during the 2015 Secret Wars comics storyline. She led A-Force in defending Arcadia, a domain on the patchwork planet Battleworld. Tatiana Maslany portrays Jennifer in the Disney+ series She-Hulk: Attorney at Law.

Amber Heard is an American actress best known for playing Mera in the DC superhero film Aquaman and its sequel. She was formerly married to actor Johnny Depp, who played Jack Sparrow in the Pirates of the Caribbean films. Their relationship became the subject of a widely publicized defamation trial in 2022. The case grew out of a 2018 opinion essay Heard wrote about speaking up against sexual violence. The essay appeared in The Washington Post, a U.S. newspaper whose slogan is “Democracy Dies in Darkness.” Although the essay did not name Depp, he sued Heard, arguing that it had damaged his reputation. The jury found that Heard had defamed Depp and also found that one statement made by Depp’s lawyer had defamed Heard.

Ted Lasso is an Apple TV+ comedy series starring Jason Sudeikis as an upbeat American football coach from Kansas. Although he knows little about association football—the sport called soccer in the United States—Ted is unexpectedly hired to manage AFC Richmond, a fictional club in south London. Richmond’s players are nicknamed the Greyhounds, and their home ground is Nelson Road. Much of the comedy comes from Ted learning a new sport and adjusting to life in England, but the show also follows the team’s friendships, rivalries and personal struggles. Ted’s optimism and concern for others help him connect with the players even when his lack of football knowledge makes him seem unqualified for the job.

Poptropica is an online role-playing game created primarily by Jeff Kinney, the author and illustrator of Diary of a Wimpy Kid. Players make a character, travel between themed islands, and solve puzzles to complete quests. Each island has its own story: Astro-Knights is a fantasy adventure, while Time Tangled involves traveling through different periods of history. Some islands are based on Kinney’s books about middle-schooler Greg Heffley. In the snowy island Wimpy Wonderland, players meet Greg and help him search for his younger brother Manny, who has disappeared. Another Diary of a Wimpy Kid-themed island is Wimpy Boardwalk. The game’s mix of exploration, stories, and puzzles lets players take part in different kinds of adventures.

The New York Times is an American newspaper and media organization founded in 1851. It is known for its reporting on news from the United States and around the world, and for its motto, “All the News That’s Fit to Print.” Alongside its journalism, the newspaper publishes games, including a daily crossword puzzle. In a crossword, players fill empty squares in a grid with words that match numbered clues. Some answers run Across the grid, while others run Down; where the words intersect, they share a letter. The New York Times crossword in the Sunday edition is especially well known. Although it is larger than the newspaper’s weekday crosswords, it uses the same basic Across-and-Down format.

The Souls series is a collection of dark-fantasy action role-playing games made by the Japanese developer FromSoftware. It began with Demon’s Souls in 2009. In that game, players explore the kingdom of Boletaria after King Allant’s pursuit of power brings a colorless fog and releases monstrous creatures. The series later expanded with the Dark Souls trilogy, whose settings include Lordran and Drangleic. Souls games are known for demanding combat: enemies can be dangerous, and players often learn by trying again after a defeat. Their bleak worlds also reward exploration, with connected areas, hidden paths, and clues about the story scattered through the environment. The games helped inspire a wider category of challenging action games called “Souls-likes,” including FromSoftware’s Bloodborne.

Jared Leto is an American actor and musician who sings lead vocals for the rock band Thirty Seconds to Mars. In the 2016 film Suicide Squad, he played the Joker, a famous comic-book villain. He later starred as the title character in Morbius, a film based on Marvel’s “Living Vampire,” a character who needs blood to survive. Leto is also associated with Method acting, a performance technique in which actors use their own emotions and experiences to help make a role feel real. Some Method actors stay immersed in their characters even when the cameras are not rolling. Knowing Leto’s film roles, his band, and the name of this acting technique helps connect the different parts of his career.

General Hospital is an American daytime soap opera that premiered in 1963. Set in the fictional city of Port Charles, it follows the personal and professional lives of people connected to its hospital and the wider community. Like many soap operas, it tells ongoing stories about relationships, family conflicts, secrets, and rivalries, alongside events involving doctors and patients. It is the longest-running American soap opera still on the air. Among its best-known characters is Sonny Corinthos, a mob boss whose storylines often connect Port Charles’s families and businesses. Actor Maurice Benard has portrayed Sonny since 1993. If a question asks for the 1963 soap opera set in Port Charles, the answer is General Hospital; if it asks who plays Sonny, the answer is Maurice Benard.

Sweet Caroline is a 1969 song written and recorded by American singer-songwriter Neil Diamond. Its warm, easy-to-sing chorus has made it a favorite at sporting events, where whole crowds often sing along. Fans add a “ba ba ba” response and join in when Diamond sings that “good times never seemed so good.” The song’s title describes Caroline as “sweet,” and its popularity as a group singalong has continued for decades. Diamond was also known for other major hits, including “Cracklin’ Rosie” and “Song Sung Blue.” If you hear a stadium crowd singing the “ba ba ba” part, the song is likely Sweet Caroline; if you are asked who wrote and recorded it, the answer is Neil Diamond.

Time travel is the fictional idea of moving to an earlier or later point in time, rather than simply going to another place. Stories may show characters using a machine to visit the past or future, or resetting events so they can experience a period again and change what happens. In the fantasy anime Re:Zero, Subaru returns to an earlier point whenever he dies, giving him another chance to act differently. In the science-fiction series Doctor Who, the Doctor travels through both time and space in a vehicle called the TARDIS. It looks like a blue police box from the outside, but its interior is famously much larger. Time-travel stories often explore what might happen if someone changes the past or learns about the future.

DC Entertainment is a Warner Bros. company that manages DC Comics characters and franchises across media, including comics, television, films, and games. DC is known for superheroes such as Superman, Batman, the Flash, and Green Arrow, and is a major rival of Marvel. One DC television series, Arrow, follows Oliver Queen, a billionaire’s son who returns to Starling City after spending five years stranded on the island of Lian Yu. He becomes a hooded vigilante who fights crime with a bow and arrows. The show is named Arrow after the projectile he shoots, not after his bow. Another television series focuses on the Flash, a superhero famous for his incredible speed. Both shows are examples of DC characters adapted for television.

Elvis Presley was an American singer and performer known as the “King of Rock and Roll.” In the 1950s, his recordings and energetic stage performances helped bring rock and roll into the mainstream. His major hits include “Heartbreak Hotel,” which describes a lonely place to stay, “Hound Dog,” and “Jailhouse Rock.” He also recorded the ballad “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” which begins with the words “Wise men say only fools rush in.” Presley became famous through records, television appearances, and movies, and his style influenced generations of musicians. In 1957, he bought Graceland, a white-columned estate in Memphis, Tennessee. He lived there until his death in 1977. Today, Graceland is a museum and the place where he is buried.

Shuri is a princess of Wakanda in Marvel’s Black Panther stories and the younger sister of T’Challa, Wakanda’s king. A brilliant inventor, she uses vibranium, a rare and powerful metal found in Wakanda, to create advanced devices, including T’Challa’s Black Panther suits. In the 2018 film Black Panther, T’Challa’s mission to stop the arms dealer Ulysses Klaue takes him to South Korea, where CIA agent Everett Ross is working undercover. Ross suffers a serious spinal injury during the mission, and T’Challa brings him to Wakanda. Shuri uses her medical technology to treat him, showing that her inventions can save lives as well as help protect her country.

Oliver Queen is the billionaire heir who becomes the bow-and-arrow-wielding vigilante known as the Arrow in the television series Arrow, based on a DC Comics character. After a shipwreck, Oliver spends five years away from his home in Starling City, much of that time on the remote island of Lian Yu. The island’s name is commonly translated as “Purgatory,” reflecting the harsh experiences that change him. When he finally returns to Starling City, he uses the survival skills and archery abilities he developed during those years to fight crime. At first, he hides his identity and works alone, but he later gains allies, including Black Canary and Spartan. Oliver’s journey from privileged heir to determined hero is central to the series.

Lawrence of Arabia is a 1962 historical epic directed by David Lean. Peter O’Toole plays T. E. Lawrence, a British officer who becomes involved in the Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire during World War I. The film is known for its vast desert landscapes and a famous match-cut: Lawrence blows out a match, and the image shifts to the sun rising over the desert. Egyptian actor Omar Sharif plays Sherif Ali, an Arab leader who becomes an important ally of Lawrence. Sharif later starred as Yuri Zhivago in another David Lean film, Doctor Zhivago. These details connect the film’s story and visual style with two of its best-known actors.

Everything Everywhere All at Once is a 2022 science-fiction comedy-drama directed by Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert. Michelle Yeoh plays Evelyn Wang, a laundromat owner whose stressful everyday life changes when Alpha Waymond, an alternate version of her husband, tells her that many parallel universes exist. This collection of universes is called the multiverse, a word also used in the title of the 2022 film Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. Evelyn discovers that other versions of herself have made different choices and developed different abilities. As she moves between realities, she faces a threat connected to Jobu Tupaki, who uses an “everything bagel” as a symbol. The film mixes action, absurd comedy, and family drama to explore choices and relationships.

Citizen Kane is a 1941 drama directed by and starring Orson Welles. It was his first feature film as a director, after he had worked in theater and radio. Welles plays Charles Foster Kane, a powerful newspaper publisher whose life is told through flashbacks after his death. Kane’s final word, “Rosebud,” puzzles a reporter, who interviews people who knew him to learn what it meant. Their memories reveal Kane’s rise to wealth and influence, as well as his troubled relationships, including his marriage to singer Susan Alexander and his years at his vast estate, Xanadu. The mystery of “Rosebud” helps the film explore how even a famous person’s life can be difficult for others to understand.

Nickelodeon is an American television network and media brand that launched nationally in 1979 as a cable channel devoted to children’s programming. Recognizable by its orange logo, it became known for cartoons such as Rugrats and SpongeBob SquarePants, as well as live-action shows such as All That. In 2005, Nickelodeon premiered the animated fantasy series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Its hero, Aang, is a boy who awakens after a century frozen in an iceberg. As the Avatar, he must learn to control all four elements—water, earth, fire, and air—and help end the Fire Nation’s war against the other nations. The series also features Azula, the daughter of Fire Lord Ozai, and was followed by another Nickelodeon animated series, The Legend of Korra.

Carmen Sandiego is a fictional globe-trotting thief and the central character of an educational entertainment franchise. Her signature red hat and coat make her easy to recognize, even as she escapes around the world. In geography-focused video games and the children’s television game show Where in the World Is Carmen Sandiego?, players use clues and their knowledge of places to track her down. The show sometimes featured guests, including Joe Biden when he was a U.S. senator from Delaware. Biden later served as vice president under Barack Obama and won the U.S. presidency in 2020. Carmen’s adventures made learning geography feel like solving an international mystery.

The Sound of Music is a 1965 musical film starring Julie Andrews as Maria, a young woman preparing to become a nun. Instead, she becomes governess to the seven children of Captain von Trapp, a widowed naval officer. Maria brings music and warmth into their home, teaching the children to sing before she and their father fall in love. Adapted from a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical, the film includes songs such as “Do-Re-Mi” and “My Favorite Things.” The story is set in Salzburg, an Austrian city near the German border that is also famous as Mozart’s birthplace. Austria’s capital is Vienna. As Nazi Germany’s influence spreads, the von Trapps face a difficult choice about their future.

Nollywood is the popular name for Nigeria’s film industry, one of the world’s largest in the number of films it produces. It grew rapidly in the early 1990s, when filmmakers began making movies for direct release on videocassette rather than showing them first in cinemas. This approach let them reach large audiences without the high costs of traditional film distribution. A landmark of this video-film boom was the 1992 Igbo-language thriller Living in Bondage. It follows Andy Okeke, who joins a secret cult in pursuit of wealth and then faces the consequences of his choice. Nollywood films have since appeared in many of Nigeria’s languages and reached audiences across Africa and beyond.

John Carpenter is an American filmmaker known for influential horror and science-fiction movies. He directed the original Halloween in 1978, a slasher film about a masked killer, and The Thing in 1982. The Thing follows an isolated research team in Antarctica as they face an alien that can imitate the people it attacks. Because anyone on the team might be the alien, the story builds fear through suspicion as well as its frightening creature effects. Carpenter’s film was inspired by the 1938 novella Who Goes There? by John W. Campbell Jr. That story had already been adapted into the 1951 film The Thing from Another World, which was produced by director Howard Hawks.

Edward Scissorhands is a 1990 fantasy-romance film directed by Tim Burton. Its main character, Edward, is an unfinished artificial man whose inventor died before giving him human hands, leaving him with scissors for fingers. A kind saleswoman brings him from his isolated mansion into her pastel-colored suburban neighborhood. Although Edward struggles to fit in, he uses his blades to create beautiful sculptures from hedges, trees, and ice, and he falls in love with the saleswoman’s daughter, Kim. Johnny Depp plays the pale, quiet Edward; years later, Depp also played Captain Jack Sparrow in the Pirates of the Caribbean films and Willy Wonka in Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. The film contrasts Edward’s gentle nature with the neighbors’ reactions to someone who looks different.

Donda is a 2021 studio album by rapper Kanye West, who is also known as Ye. He named it after his mother, Donda West, whose life and memory are important themes on the album. Its opening track, “Donda Chant,” repeats her name in a rhythm resembling a heartbeat. West built excitement for the release with large listening events, including events at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, where he also worked on the music. The album mixes hip-hop with gospel influences and features many guest artists. One of its best-known tracks is “Jail,” which includes a guest verse from fellow rapper Jay-Z. “Jail” won the Grammy Award for Best Rap Song.

James Stewart, often called Jimmy Stewart, was an American actor known for playing thoughtful, ordinary people caught in difficult situations. He served as a bomber pilot during World War II and became one of classic Hollywood’s leading stars. One of his best-known roles was George Bailey in It’s a Wonderful Life. In Alfred Hitchcock’s Vertigo, Stewart plays John “Scottie” Ferguson, a former San Francisco detective whose fear of heights complicates his investigation of a woman named Madeleine Elster. As Scottie follows her, he becomes caught in an unsettling mystery. Vertigo is famous for its spiraling opening titles and for a camera effect called the dolly zoom, which makes the view down a mission bell tower appear to stretch away.

Eddie Munson, played by Joseph Quinn, is a Hawkins High senior introduced in the fourth season of Stranger Things. He leads the Hellfire Club, a Dungeons & Dragons group, and plays guitar in the heavy-metal band Corroded Coffin. When fellow student Chrissy Cunningham is killed by the villain Vecna in Eddie’s trailer, people in Hawkins suspect Eddie, even though he did not kill her. Dustin Henderson and his friends work with him to confront the real threat. In the season finale, Eddie climbs onto a trailer in the Upside Down and plays Metallica’s “Master of Puppets” on electric guitar. The loud music draws a swarm of batlike creatures called demobats away from his friends, giving them a chance to carry out their plan.

Justin Bieber is a Canadian pop singer who first attracted attention when his mother uploaded videos of his performances to YouTube. He became a global teenage star with the 2010 single “Baby,” which features a rap verse by Ludacris. An Atlanta-born rapper, Ludacris had earlier found mainstream success with albums including Back for the First Time and Word of Mouf and singles such as “Stand Up” and “Rollout (My Business).” Bieber went on to release hits including “Love Yourself” and “Ghost,” which includes the line “I miss you more than life.” He also collaborated with The Kid LAROI on “STAY” and joined Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee on a remix of “Despacito.”

Walter White is the main character of the television drama Breaking Bad. At the start of the series, he is a high-school chemistry teacher in Albuquerque, New Mexico. After learning that he has lung cancer, Walter decides to manufacture methamphetamine, an illegal drug, hoping to leave money for his family. He teams up with Jesse Pinkman, a former student who is now a small-time drug dealer, and they begin cooking meth in an RV. Walter’s chemistry skills help them make a product known as “Blue Sky.” As their business expands, Walter becomes a powerful and dangerous figure in the drug trade, sometimes using the name Heisenberg. Jesse, meanwhile, grows increasingly disturbed by the violence and harm their operation causes.

Supercell is a mobile-game studio founded in 2010 and headquartered in Helsinki, Finland. It developed Clash of Clans, a strategy game in which players build a village, upgrade its Town Hall, and raid other villages for resources such as gold and elixir. Players can also join clans and fight clan wars. Supercell released another game, Clash Royale, in 2016. Although it shares characters with Clash of Clans, Clash Royale plays differently: players use collectible cards to deploy troops and spells during short, real-time arena battles. The aim is to destroy an opponent’s crown towers, including the central King Tower, while defending your own. Both games feature the yellow-haired Barbarian, one of Supercell’s most recognizable characters.

Hades is a 2020 roguelike action game developed by Supergiant Games. You play as Zagreus, a young prince of the Greek underworld, who repeatedly fights his way toward the surface to escape his father, Hades, the underworld’s ruler. Each attempt takes Zagreus through changing rooms filled with enemies, and defeat sends him back to the House of Hades to prepare for another run. In the House’s courtyard, a friendly skeleton named Skelly lets players test weapons by attacking him. If Zagreus gives Skelly a gift called Nectar, Skelly gives him the Lucky Tooth, a keepsake that restores some health when Zagreus would otherwise die. The game draws on Greek mythology for its characters, locations, and weapons, including the Eternal Spear and Adamant Rail.

Welcome to Wrexham is an FX documentary series about Wrexham A.F.C., a soccer club in Wales. It follows actors Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds as they buy the club and try to revive its fortunes. Reynolds is a Canadian actor also known for playing the superhero Deadpool. The series shows that owning a football club involves more than cheering from the stands: the new owners must make decisions about the team, connect with supporters, and learn why the club matters so much to the town of Wrexham. In Wales, the sport is usually called football; in North America, it is commonly called soccer. The documentary’s title, Welcome to Wrexham, refers to the town where the club is based.

The Twilight Zone is an American anthology television series created and hosted by Rod Serling that originally ran from 1959 to 1964. An anthology tells a different story in each episode, often with new characters and actors. The show blends science fiction, supernatural events, and psychological drama, usually ending with an unsettling twist that makes viewers question what is real. In “Judgment Night,” a passenger on a ship discovers that he is a U-boat captain being punished for war crimes. Another famous episode, “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet,” stars William Shatner as an airline passenger who sees a creature damaging the plane from its wing, though nobody else can confirm what he sees. Jordan Peele narrated a 2019 revival of the series.

Zero Dark Thirty is a 2012 historical drama directed by Kathryn Bigelow. It follows the CIA’s years-long search for Osama bin Laden, the al-Qaeda leader responsible for the September 11, 2001, attacks in the United States. Much of the film focuses on analysts piecing together clues about bin Laden’s possible hiding place. That trail leads to a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, where U.S. forces killed him during a nighttime raid in 2011. The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Picture, but it also sparked debate because of its scenes showing CIA interrogations. Critics argued that it appeared to suggest torture helped locate bin Laden, a claim that has been strongly disputed.

FIFA was a long-running soccer video-game series published by EA Sports. Its name came from FIFA, the international organization that governs soccer and organizes the men’s and women’s World Cups. The games let players control real-world clubs and national teams, compete in matches, and build squads using familiar players. Music was also part of the experience: FIFA 19, the installment released in 2018 for the 2019 season, included “you should see me in a crown” on its soundtrack. That song is by Billie Eilish, the singer also known for “bad guy” and “everything i wanted.” Eilish later wrote and performed the title song for No Time to Die, a James Bond film starring Daniel Craig. EA Sports now releases its soccer games under the EA Sports FC name rather than FIFA.

Timothée Chalamet is an American actor known for playing thoughtful, ambitious young characters in films based on well-known books. In Denis Villeneuve’s Dune, adapted from Frank Herbert’s science-fiction novel, he plays Paul Atreides, the young heir of Duke Leto and House Atreides. Paul’s family is sent to govern Arrakis, a desert planet where workers harvest spice, an extremely valuable substance used in space travel. Chalamet also plays Theodore “Laurie” Laurence in Greta Gerwig’s adaptation of Little Women. Laurie is close to the March sisters, especially Jo. Another of Chalamet’s major roles is Elio Perlman in Call Me by Your Name, a coming-of-age film about first love. If a question mentions Paul, Laurie, and Elio together, the actor is Timothée Chalamet.

Scarface: The Shame of the Nation is a 1932 gangster film directed by Howard Hawks and produced by Howard Hughes. It follows Tony Camonte, an ambitious criminal whose violent rise to power was loosely modeled on the real-life gangster Al Capone. The film appeared when stories about organized crime were popular in American movies, but its violence also made it controversial. Hawks worked across many genres: he directed the comedies Bringing Up Baby and His Girl Friday, and later directed Lauren Bacall opposite Humphrey Bogart in To Have and Have Not. A much later film, Scarface (1983), reused the title and the basic idea of a criminal’s rise and fall, but starred Al Pacino as a Cuban drug lord named Tony Montana.

Stand-up comedy is a live performance in which a comedian speaks directly to an audience, usually on a club or theater stage, to make people laugh. Unlike an actor in a play, the comedian typically performs as themselves, telling jokes, sharing stories, making observations, or responding to the crowd. Some comedians, such as Steven Wright and Mitch Hedberg, are known for short jokes with surprising endings. Stand-up can also address serious experiences through humor. In 2012, American comedian Tig Notaro performed an acclaimed set at Largo in Los Angeles shortly after being diagnosed with breast cancer. She opened by candidly telling the audience about her diagnosis, and the performance was later released as the album Live.

Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu, later known simply as Ninjago, is an animated television series based on Lego’s ninja-themed toys. It follows a team of young ninja who learn Spinjitzu, a powerful martial art, and use elemental abilities to protect their world. Their elderly mentor, Master Wu, brings the team together and trains them aboard their flying ship, Destiny’s Bounty. Wu is the son of the First Spinjitzu Master and the younger brother of Lord Garmadon, whose shifting loyalties make him both an enemy and an ally. Recognizable by his staff and his fondness for tea, Wu guides the ninja as they face threats ranging from serpentine warriors to ghosts and other supernatural villains.

Wild Strawberries is a 1957 Swedish film directed by Ingmar Bergman. It follows Isak Borg, an elderly retired professor played by Victor Sjöström, who was also a silent-film director. Borg travels to the city of Lund to receive an honorary degree, but the journey becomes more than a celebration of his career. People and places he encounters bring back memories of his youth, while unsettling dreams make him think about aging, loneliness, and the choices he has made. As he reflects on his relationships with family and others, he begins to question whether his professional success has come at the cost of personal connection. The film uses his road trip to explore how remembering the past can change the way someone understands their life.

Natalie Portman is an actress known for roles in romantic comedies, historical dramas, science fiction, and superhero films. In No Strings Attached, she plays Emma Kurtzman, a doctor who agrees to a relationship without romance with a friend played by Ashton Kutcher. She portrays former First Lady Jackie Kennedy in Jackie and Padmé Amidala in the Star Wars prequel trilogy. Portman also plays Evey Hammond in the 2005 dystopian film V for Vendetta, adapted from a graphic novel by Alan Moore and David Lloyd. In that story, Evey is rescued from secret police by V, a masked revolutionary fighting to overthrow a totalitarian British government. In the Thor films, Portman plays Jane Foster, a scientist connected to the Norse thunder god.

Gordon Ramsay is a Scottish celebrity chef and television personality known for his sharp critiques, fiery temper, and sometimes foul-mouthed outbursts. He hosts cooking shows such as Hell’s Kitchen, where chefs compete under pressure, and Kitchen Nightmares, where he helps struggling restaurants improve. Ramsay also appeared on Hot Ones, an interview show hosted by Sean Evans in which guests answer questions while eating ten wings coated in increasingly spicy sauces. Ramsay brought items such as lemon and lime juice to help him cope with the heat. The wings he and Evans ate were chicken wings. Buffalo, New York, gives its name to Buffalo wings, a popular way of preparing chicken wings with a spicy sauce.

Lucille Ball was an American comedian and actress who became a television pioneer as Lucy Ricardo in the 1950s sitcom I Love Lucy. Lucy’s attempts to try new jobs and get into show business often went hilariously wrong. In one famous scene, she tries to sell a health tonic called Vitameatavegamin but becomes increasingly tipsy while rehearsing its sales pitch. In another, she and her friend Ethel struggle to keep up with chocolates moving along a factory conveyor belt. Ball starred opposite her real-life husband, Desi Arnaz, a Cuban-born musician and bandleader who played Lucy’s on-screen husband, Ricky Ricardo. Arnaz also helped popularize the conga line in the United States. Ball’s expressive physical comedy made I Love Lucy one of television’s most influential sitcoms.

2001: A Space Odyssey is a 1968 science-fiction film directed by Stanley Kubrick. It explores human evolution, space travel, and the risks of artificial intelligence. Early in the film, an ape discovers how to use a bone as a tool while Richard Strauss’s “Also sprach Zarathustra” plays. The ape tosses the bone into the air, and a famous match cut jumps to a spacecraft in orbit, connecting the first tools with future technology. Later, astronauts travel aboard the spacecraft Discovery One. Its onboard computer, HAL 9000, manages the ship and even plays chess with astronaut Frank Poole. HAL becomes dangerous when it resists the crew’s efforts to disconnect it. The film is also known for its striking images and its use of music by composer György Ligeti.

Bored Ape Yacht Club is a collection of 10,000 non-fungible tokens, or NFTs, launched in April 2021. Each token is linked to a cartoon portrait of a “bored” ape with a different combination of features, such as clothing, expressions, and backgrounds. An NFT is a digital record that can show who owns a particular item; the Bored Ape tokens are recorded on the Ethereum blockchain. Ethereum is a network that supports smart contracts, which are programs that can carry out transactions, and its native cryptocurrency is called ether. Owning a Bored Ape also gave holders access to members-only online features, including a communal graffiti wall called the Bathroom, where they could add marks to a shared digital canvas. The collection became widely known through celebrity purchases and online discussion.

Arrow is a television superhero drama based on DC Comics’ Green Arrow. Its main character, Oliver Queen, is the son of a billionaire from Starling City. After being stranded for five years on the remote island of Lian Yu, he returns home with new survival and archery skills. Oliver becomes a masked, green-cloaked vigilante who uses a bow and arrows to fight crime and protect his city. The series is called Arrow after his signature weapon, while Oliver Queen is the hero’s civilian name. As the story develops, allies including Black Canary and Spartan help him face dangerous enemies.

Pat Buchanan is an American conservative commentator who worked in Republican politics and ran for president. At the 1992 Republican National Convention, he gave a speech warning that the United States was in a “culture war” over social values, including questions about religion, women’s roles, and gay rights. He later became the Reform Party’s presidential nominee in 2000. Buchanan also appeared on television to debate current events: he and liberal journalist Michael Kinsley represented opposing viewpoints as co-hosts of CNN’s Crossfire. The program brought people with different political opinions together to argue about issues in the news.
