Pat Buchanan is not the same person as James Buchanan, the U.S. president who served just before the Civil War.

A Quarter Quell is a special edition of the Hunger Games held every twenty-five years in Suzanne Collins’s series. In the future country of Panem, the Capitol normally forces children from its districts to fight in an arena, but each Quarter Quell adds a new rule to the competition. In the first Quarter Quell, districts had to vote on which children would be sent as tributes. The 75th Hunger Games, or third Quarter Quell, required previous winners to compete again, even though they had already survived an earlier Games. This rule sends Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark back to the Capitol and into the arena. Their return is a major part of Catching Fire, the second novel in the Hunger Games trilogy.

Fly Me to the Moon is a popular standard written by Bart Howard. It was first recorded in 1954 under the title In Other Words, but listeners came to know it by the opening line, “Fly me to the moon.” The song uses space travel as a playful way to express love: the singer asks to see what spring is like on Jupiter and Mars, then asks a beloved to “fill my heart with song and let me sing forevermore.” Many performers have recorded it, but one of the best-known versions is by Frank Sinatra. He recorded it for his 1964 album It Might as Well Be Swing, backed by Count Basie’s orchestra, with an arrangement by Quincy Jones.

In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the Infinity Stones are six differently colored gems with extraordinary control over fundamental aspects of existence: space, time, reality, power, mind, and soul. Thanos gathers them in a powerful glove called the Infinity Gauntlet; with all six, he can erase half of all life with a snap of his fingers. Each stone also has its own story. The blue Space Stone was hidden inside the Tesseract and can move its bearer across vast distances or open portals. HYDRA pursued the Tesseract during World War II, and Loki later used it to bring the Chitauri army to Earth. The green Time Stone was kept in the Eye of Agamotto, while obtaining the Soul Stone required a sacrifice on Vormir.

Slender Man is a fictional horror figure who began as an Internet creation rather than an old legend. In 2009, artist Eric Knudsen used the pseudonym Victor Surge to post manipulated photographs in a Photoshop contest on the Something Awful forum. The images showed an unnaturally tall, thin man with a blank, featureless face and a dark suit, often appearing near children. Other Internet users added stories, pictures, and videos, turning him into a shared piece of online folklore. In those stories, Slender Man often stalks people in wooded places and may have unusually long arms or tentacle-like limbs. His popularity led to horror games, videos, and other fiction. Despite the realistic style of some early images, Slender Man was invented for the contest.

Sasuke Uchiha is a central character in Naruto, a Japanese anime and manga series about young ninjas. He is one of the few survivors of the Uchiha clan massacre, in which his parents and many other relatives were killed. Sasuke possesses the Sharingan, a powerful sight ability passed down through his clan that helps him perceive and respond to an opponent’s movements. The person who carried out the massacre was Sasuke’s older brother, Itachi Uchiha. Believing Itachi had betrayed their family, Sasuke spends much of the story training and seeking revenge against him. He later learns that Itachi acted to prevent a planned Uchiha rebellion and protect their village, making the brothers’ conflict more complicated than it first appeared.

Queen is a British rock band formed in London in 1970. Its four members were Freddie Mercury, the lead singer and pianist; Brian May, the guitarist; Roger Taylor, the drummer; and John Deacon, the bassist. The band became famous for powerful vocals, layered harmonies, and songs that mix different musical styles. Its hits include “We Are the Champions” and “Another One Bites the Dust.” One of Queen’s best-known songs, “Bohemian Rhapsody,” lasts nearly six minutes and does not follow a typical verse-and-chorus pattern. It begins with a piano-led ballad, moves through a Brian May electric-guitar solo into an operatic section with repeated calls of “Galileo,” then shifts to hard rock before ending quietly. Its elaborate sound helped make it a landmark rock recording.

Dune is a 2021 science-fiction film directed by Denis Villeneuve and adapted from Frank Herbert’s influential novel. It follows Paul Atreides, the young heir to House Atreides, as his family takes control of Arrakis, a harsh desert planet. Arrakis is the only source of spice, also called melange, an extraordinarily valuable substance that makes space travel possible. Huge machines called crawlers harvest spice from the desert, but rival powers want to control it, drawing Paul and his family into a dangerous conflict. Paul is played by Timothée Chalamet, who also portrayed Elio Perlman in Call Me by Your Name and Laurie in Little Women.

Harry’s House is the third solo studio album by British singer-songwriter Harry Styles, who first became famous as a member of One Direction. Released on May 20, 2022, it followed his album Fine Line, which included the hit “Watermelon Sugar.” Harry’s House mixes pop with dance music and other styles, pairing catchy sounds with lyrics about relationships, change, and everyday life. Its lead single, “As It Was,” arrived in April 2022, before the album came out. With its bright, synth-led hook, the song became a global hit and spent 15 nonconsecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. If a question asks for Styles’s 2022 album “house,” the answer is Harry’s House; if it asks for the album’s record-setting lead single, it is “As It Was.”

Spock is a central character in Star Trek: The Original Series, a 1960s science-fiction television show about the crew of the starship USS Enterprise. Played by Leonard Nimoy, Spock serves as the ship’s science officer and Captain James T. Kirk’s first officer, or second-in-command. His father, Sarek, is Vulcan, and his mother, Amanda Grayson, is human. Spock is known for valuing logic over emotion, though his mixed heritage sometimes puts those sides of his identity in tension. As members of Starfleet, Spock and the Enterprise crew are expected to follow the Prime Directive. This rule forbids them from interfering with the natural development of other civilizations, even when they believe they could help.

Isle of Dogs is a 2018 animated comedy film directed by Wes Anderson. In its fictional Japanese city, a scare about canine flu leads the authorities to exile every dog to a landfill island. A boy named Atari travels to the island to find Spots, the dog that once served as his bodyguard. The film uses stop-motion animation: filmmakers photograph physical puppets, move them slightly, and take another picture. When the images are played quickly in sequence, the figures appear to move on their own. This technique lets the filmmakers create the dogs, the trash-covered island, and the story’s action using real miniature models rather than drawings or computer-generated characters.

Cats is a stage musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber, based on T. S. Eliot’s poetry collection Old Possum’s Book of Practical Cats. It follows the Jellicles, a tribe of cats who gather for the Jellicle Ball. During the night, their leader, Old Deuteronomy, must choose one cat to ascend to the Heaviside Layer and begin a new life. The cats introduce themselves through songs and dances, but Grizabella, a once-glamorous cat, is shunned because she is old and worn down. When she sings the musical’s best-known song, “Memory,” the others finally welcome her back. Old Deuteronomy chooses Grizabella, and she ascends to the Heaviside Layer at the end of the show.

Red Skull is a Marvel Comics supervillain and one of Captain America’s oldest enemies. His original identity is Johann Schmidt, a Nazi agent whose frightening skull-like appearance inspired his villain name. Captain America, also known as Steve Rogers, gained his abilities through the super-soldier program called Operation Rebirth and fought Red Skull during World War II. Their rivalry has continued in stories set long after the war. Red Skull often seeks extraordinary power so he can control others, and he has repeatedly tried to use an artifact called the Cosmic Cube. The Cube can alter reality, making it dangerous in the hands of someone with his ambitions. In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the artifact is known as the Tesseract.

Reddit is an online platform where people share links, images, questions, and text posts in communities devoted to particular interests. These communities are called subreddits and have names beginning with “r/,” such as r/quizbowl for people interested in quizbowl. Members can comment on posts and upvote or downvote contributions; posts with more upvotes often become more prominent. One well-known Reddit event is r/place, a collaborative art project built around a shared pixel canvas. During the event, users could place one colored pixel at a time, then had to wait before placing another. Groups worked together to make flags, memes, and detailed pictures, while sometimes competing with other groups for space.

Dr. Dre is an American rapper, record producer, and entrepreneur born in Compton, California. As a member of N.W.A., he helped define West Coast gangsta rap, and his 1992 solo album The Chronic became a landmark in hip-hop. He later founded Aftermath Entertainment, a record label that helped launch and develop other artists’ careers, including Eminem’s. Dr. Dre was the focal point of the 2022 Super Bowl halftime show, which brought together several major hip-hop performers. During the show, Snoop Dogg played the famous piano riff from “Still D.R.E.” Another performer was Eminem, a Detroit rapper who performed his hit “Lose Yourself” and took a knee afterward. Eminem also played the character Rabbit in the film 8 Mile.

Stephen Colbert is an American comedian and television host known for using satire to comment on politics and the news. After working as a correspondent on The Daily Show, he hosted Comedy Central’s The Colbert Report, where he played an exaggerated conservative television pundit. The character confidently defended ideas that the real Colbert was often mocking, making the show a popular example of political satire. In 2015, Colbert succeeded David Letterman as host of CBS’s The Late Show. He also drew widespread attention for his speech at the 2006 White House Correspondents’ Dinner, an annual Washington gathering of journalists and political figures. Speaking while George W. Bush was president, Colbert delivered a sharply satirical roast of Bush. The dinner traditionally features a comedian alongside remarks from the sitting president.

The Hunt for Red October is a 1990 submarine thriller directed by John McTiernan, based on Tom Clancy’s novel. Sean Connery plays Marko Ramius, a Lithuanian-born captain in the Soviet navy who takes a powerful submarine called Red October toward the United States. American and Soviet forces are unsure whether he plans to attack or defect, making his intentions the central mystery of the film. Alec Baldwin plays CIA analyst Jack Ryan, who tries to work out what Ramius is doing before either side makes a dangerous mistake. Ryan first appeared in Clancy’s 1984 novel The Hunt for Red October and became a recurring character in his books and their film adaptations. The film combines underwater action with Cold War tension, when distrust between the United States and the Soviet Union shaped world politics.

Star Wars is a 1977 space-opera film written and directed by George Lucas. It follows Luke Skywalker, a young farmhand who joins the Rebel Alliance in its fight against the Galactic Empire. With help from friends and mentors, Luke helps destroy the Death Star, the Empire’s planet-killing battle station. The film introduced audiences to the villain Darth Vader and launched a major film saga. Lucas shaped Luke’s journey using Joseph Campbell’s “monomyth,” a storytelling pattern in which an ordinary person answers a call to adventure and grows through challenges. He also drew inspiration from classic adventure serials and Japanese samurai cinema, including Akira Kurosawa’s The Hidden Fortress. Before making Star Wars, Lucas had written and directed American Graffiti.

We Bare Bears is an animated television series about three bear brothers trying to fit into everyday life in the San Francisco Bay Area. Grizzly, often called Grizz, is the oldest and an energetic grizzly bear. Panda is a bamboo-eating panda who loves his phone and often worries about what others think. Ice Bear is a white polar bear who speaks about himself in the third person, saying “Ice Bear” instead of “I.” He is also skilled at cooking and martial arts. The brothers share adventures involving friendships, technology, and the challenges of living among humans. One of their most recognizable habits is the “bear stack”: they travel around town with Grizz on top, Panda in the middle, and Ice Bear at the bottom.

Billy Joel is an American singer-songwriter and pianist who was born in the Bronx, New York. Many of his songs tell stories through memorable characters and lyrics. His 1973 song “Piano Man” draws on his experience playing at a Los Angeles bar called the Executive Room. Its verses introduce regulars including John the bartender and Davy, a sailor, while the chorus asks the pianist for a melody that will make everyone feel all right. Joel’s 1983 hit “Uptown Girl” is about a wealthy young woman attracted to a man from a different social world. In his 1989 hit “We Didn’t Start the Fire,” rapid-fire lyrics name people and events from the presidency of Harry Truman through the late 1980s.

Bobby Brown is an American R&B singer who began his career in the Boston vocal group New Edition. After leaving the group, he became a solo star in the late 1980s with songs such as “My Prerogative” and “On Our Own,” the theme song for the film Ghostbusters II. His solo music helped bring New Jack Swing into mainstream pop. Popularized by producer Teddy Riley, New Jack Swing blended smooth R&B singing with funk-inspired grooves and the drum machines and production techniques of hip-hop. Its energetic, danceable sound became a major influence on pop and R&B around the turn of the 1990s. Bobby Brown shares his surname with James Brown, an earlier funk pioneer, but they are different performers.

Bloodborne is an action role-playing game made by the Japanese company FromSoftware, also known for the Souls series and Elden Ring. You play as a hunter who arrives in Yharnam, a Gothic city of towering buildings, dark streets, and frightening secrets. A mysterious illness has spread through the city, transforming many infected residents into monstrous beasts. As the hunter searches for a cure and tries to uncover the cause of the disaster, you explore dangerous areas and fight creatures and powerful bosses. Bloodborne is often called a “Souls-like” game because it shares the challenging combat and careful exploration associated with FromSoftware’s Souls games. Its mix of horror, mystery, and difficult battles makes Yharnam central to the experience.

A tabloid is a newspaper format with pages smaller than those of a traditional broadsheet, making it easier to hold and read. Tabloids are often associated with short stories, large photos, celebrity gossip, and punchy or sensational headlines designed to grab attention. The word describes the paper’s physical size, though it is also used for this style of journalism. One well-known example is the New York Post, an American newspaper founded by Alexander Hamilton in 1801 and now owned by Rupert Murdoch. The Post runs the Page Six gossip column and is famous for bold front-page headlines. Another example is Britain’s Daily Mirror. Not every small-format newspaper relies on sensational stories, but the connection between tabloids and attention-grabbing news is common.

Willie Nelson is an American country singer-songwriter and guitarist born in Abbott, Texas. His songs “On the Road Again” and “Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain” helped make him one of country music’s best-known figures. He became a leader of outlaw country, a movement whose musicians wanted more freedom from the polished sound and strict rules of the Nashville music industry. Nelson also helped start Farm Aid in 1985 with Neil Young and John Mellencamp. The organization holds concerts to raise money and awareness for family farmers. For decades, Nelson has played the same Martin N-20 acoustic guitar, which he nicknamed Trigger. Its worn appearance, including a large hole in the soundboard, shows how much he has used it throughout his career.

Ms. Marvel is a six-episode Marvel Cinematic Universe television series that debuted on Disney+ in June 2022. It follows Kamala Khan, a Pakistani-American teenager living in Jersey City who loves superheroes, especially Captain Marvel. After putting on a mysterious golden bangle, Kamala discovers that she can create glowing shapes and structures with her powers. As she learns to use them, she also explores her family’s history and what it means to be a hero. Kamala is played by Iman Vellani, a Pakistani-Canadian performer who made her screen-acting debut in the series. Vellani later reprised the role in the MCU film The Marvels.

Studio Ghibli is a Japanese animation studio founded in 1985 by filmmakers Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata and producer Toshio Suzuki. It is known for imaginative hand-drawn films that combine memorable characters, detailed fantasy worlds, and themes such as growing up and caring for nature. One of its most acclaimed films is Spirited Away, released in 2001 and directed by Miyazaki. It follows Chihiro, a ten-year-old girl who enters a spirit world after her parents are transformed into pigs. To survive and find a way to save them, she takes a job at a bathhouse for spirits, where she is given the new name Sen. Along the way, she encounters unusual beings, including No-Face, while learning to be brave and resourceful.

Pac-Man is a classic arcade maze game released in 1980. Its title character is a round yellow figure who travels through corridors eating dots, also called pellets, while avoiding four colored ghosts. Eating a power pellet lets Pac-Man chase and eat the ghosts for a short time. Bonus items such as cherries and strawberries sometimes appear in the maze and give extra points when collected. The arcade follow-up Ms. Pac-Man centers on Pac-Man’s wife, who navigates mazes and dodges ghosts in much the same way. Along with familiar fruit, Ms. Pac-Man adds new bonus items, including pretzels, pears, and bananas. If a question describes the original yellow dot-eater, the answer is Pac-Man; if it asks about his wife’s game, the answer is Ms. Pac-Man.

Kendrick Lamar is an American rapper and songwriter born in Compton, California. His music often explores identity, racism, community, and the pressures of fame through vivid storytelling. His third studio album, To Pimp a Butterfly, was released in 2015 and blends hip-hop with jazz, funk, and spoken-word poetry. It opens with “Wesley’s Theory” and includes the singles “King Kunta” and “Alright,” the latter of which became an anthem at protests against racial injustice. Lamar also appeared on We Got It from Here…, the final album by the influential hip-hop group A Tribe Called Quest. In 2018, he became the first rapper to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music, receiving it for his album DAMN.

“Let It Go” is a power ballad from Disney’s 2013 animated film Frozen. Elsa sings it after leaving her kingdom and climbing into the mountains, where she uses her ice powers to build a palace. The song expresses her relief at no longer having to hide those powers, even as she chooses to live apart from others. Its closing line, “The cold never bothered me anyway,” became especially famous. “Let It Go” won the Academy Award for Best Original Song. It was performed for the film by Idina Menzel, the Broadway performer who voiced Elsa in both Frozen and Frozen II. Menzel also originated the role of Elphaba in the Broadway musical Wicked.

Ben Shapiro is an American conservative political commentator, author, and lawyer known for his writing, debates, and media appearances. At age 17, he became the youngest nationally syndicated columnist in the United States, meaning his columns appeared in newspapers across the country. He has written nonfiction books and the political novel True Allegiance. Shapiro is also associated with the phrase “facts don’t care about your feelings,” which he uses to emphasize his view that evidence should matter more than emotion in arguments. In 2015, he and filmmaker Jeremy Boreing launched The Daily Wire, a conservative media company. It began as a news and commentary outlet and later expanded into podcasts, books, and streaming entertainment.

The Barbarian is a signature troop in Supercell’s mobile game Clash of Clans. With bright yellow hair and a sword, he appears on the game’s app icon. Barbarians fight at close range on the ground, so they must reach an enemy before they can attack. The troop also appears in Clash Royale, another Supercell game in which players use collectible cards to defend their towers and attack opponents. In Clash of Clans, players build a village, upgrade their Town Hall, and raid for resources such as gold and elixir. As the village grows, players can unlock the Barbarian King at Town Hall 7. This powerful, durable melee hero is the Barbarian’s heroic counterpart.

The Eye of Agamotto is a mystical relic that Doctor Strange wears as a pendant. In Marvel comics, it is associated with powerful magic and helps him uncover hidden truths. In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the Eye holds the green Time Stone, one of six Infinity Stones that control different aspects of the universe. Doctor Strange uses the Time Stone to manipulate time: while learning to use it, he reverses the decay of an apple, and he later uses its power during his confrontation with Dormammu. The other stones govern space, reality, power, mind, and soul. Thanos seeks all six because, together, they give him enough power to erase half of all life with a snap of his fingers.

Carrie Underwood is an American country singer who became famous after winning the fourth season of American Idol in 2005. Her powerful voice and songs that tell vivid stories helped make her one of country music’s biggest stars. In “Before He Cheats,” she sings about discovering that a boyfriend has been unfaithful, while “Cowboy Casanova” warns about a charming but dangerous man. Her 2012 album Blown Away includes “See You Again,” a song that offers comfort after the death of a loved one. Its message is that saying goodbye is painful, but the separation may not be forever. Underwood’s “See You Again” is different from songs with the same title by Miley Cyrus and by Wiz Khalifa featuring Charlie Puth.

Top Gun is a 1986 American action film about U.S. Navy fighter pilots training at an elite naval aviation school. Tom Cruise plays Pete “Maverick” Mitchell, a talented but reckless trainee whose callsign suits his independent streak. He competes with other pilots while learning to work as part of a team and coping with the death of his friend and flight partner, “Goose.” Maverick also begins a romance with Charlotte “Charlie” Blackwood, a civilian instructor at the school. Their relationship is accompanied by Berlin’s power ballad “Take My Breath Away,” which won the Academy Award for Best Original Song. The film’s fast-paced flying scenes, music, and memorable characters made it a major hit.

Wolf Blitzer is an American television journalist who joined CNN in 1990 and became one of the network’s longtime anchors. He is best known for hosting The Situation Room, a news program that covers major events, politics, and breaking stories. CNN, which stands for Cable News Network, was founded by Ted Turner and launched in 1980 as a 24-hour television news channel. That meant viewers could watch news throughout the day rather than waiting for a scheduled evening broadcast. Blitzer’s long career at CNN has made him a familiar face in American television news. If a quiz asks who hosts The Situation Room, the answer is Wolf Blitzer; if it asks which network carries the show, the answer is CNN.

Disney+ is a subscription streaming service run by the Walt Disney Company. Launched in the United States in November 2019, it offers Disney films and shows alongside Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) and Star Wars stories. It is also home to original series, including Ms. Marvel, a six-episode show that premiered in summer 2022. The series follows Kamala Khan, a teenager from Jersey City who admires superheroes and gains powers after putting on a golden bangle. Pakistani-Canadian actor Iman Vellani plays Kamala, also known as Ms. Marvel. The role was Vellani’s screen-acting debut, meaning it was her first credited performance in a film or television show.

Finneas O’Connell is an American singer-songwriter, musician, and record producer best known for working with his younger sister, pop singer Billie Eilish. The two write songs together, and Finneas often produces her recordings, helping shape their distinctive sound. He co-wrote and produced much of Billie’s 2019 debut studio album, When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?, which includes “bad guy,” “bury a friend,” and “when the party’s over.” Their collaborations also include “You Should See Me in a Crown” and “Wish You Were Gay.” Finneas releases music under his own name, too: his solo songs include “Break My Heart Again” and “Let’s Fall in Love for the Night.” Although he often works behind the scenes, his songwriting and production have made him an important figure in modern pop music.

Akira Kurosawa was a Japanese director whose films influenced filmmakers around the world. In Seven Samurai (1954), a farming village hires seven masterless warriors, called ronin, to protect it from bandits. Kurosawa also turned Shakespeare’s Macbeth into Throne of Blood, a story of ambition and betrayal set among samurai. His adventure film The Hidden Fortress, which follows two quarrelling peasants caught up in a struggle involving a princess, helped inspire Star Wars. Another famous film, Rashomon (1950), presents conflicting accounts of a killing from a bandit, a woman, a murdered samurai speaking through a medium, and a woodcutter. The Rashomon effect is named after this film: it describes how different people can give incompatible versions of the same event.

“Take My Breath Away” is a 1986 song recorded by the band Berlin and used as a love theme in the film Top Gun. The movie follows U.S. Navy fighter pilots training at an elite school, including Pete “Maverick” Mitchell, played by Tom Cruise. The song accompanies Maverick’s romance with instructor Charlie Blackwood, giving the action-packed film a quieter, emotional moment. “Take My Breath Away” was co-written and produced by Giorgio Moroder, an Italian composer known for electronic music and film soundtracks. His other film work includes Midnight Express and Flashdance. The song became one of the best-known parts of Top Gun’s soundtrack and won the Academy Award for Best Original Song.

Sinnoh is a fictional region in the Pokémon world, modeled primarily on Hokkaido, Japan’s northernmost main island. It is the setting of the Generation IV games Pokémon Diamond and Pearl, as well as their Nintendo Switch remakes, Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl. Pokémon Legends: Arceus explores the same region in the distant past, when it was called Hisui. A major landmark in Sinnoh is Mount Coronet, a mountain range that runs through the middle of the region and separates its eastern and western sides. At its summit is Spear Pillar, an ancient site where players can encounter the legendary Pokémon Dialga in Diamond or Palkia in Pearl. These places and Pokémon are central to Sinnoh’s story.

The Longest Yard is a 1974 American sports film directed by Robert Aldrich, who also directed The Dirty Dozen and The Flight of the Phoenix. Burt Reynolds stars as Paul Crewe, a disgraced former professional American-football quarterback who ends up in prison. There, Crewe helps assemble a team of inmates to play a game against the prison guards. The players must learn to work together while facing opponents who have power over their daily lives. The film mixes football action and comedy with a story about standing up to authority. In 2005, The Longest Yard was remade with Adam Sandler playing Crewe and Reynolds appearing in a different role. If asked to identify the 1974 prison football film, the answer is The Longest Yard; its director was Robert Aldrich.

Sigur Rós is an Icelandic post-rock band known for creating spacious, emotional music. Its singer, Jónsi, often sings in a high falsetto and plays guitar with a bow, producing long, sustained sounds rather than ordinary strummed chords. The band’s album titled ( ) contains eight untitled tracks arranged in two groups of four, separated by 36 seconds of silence. On that album, Jónsi sang in Hopelandic, an invented vocal language whose sounds fit the music rather than communicate fixed words. These clues—the bowed guitar, falsetto singing, unusual album structure, and Hopelandic vocals—help identify Sigur Rós and distinguish its music from that of other Icelandic artists.

Random Access Memories is the fourth studio album by Daft Punk, the French electronic music duo famous for performing in helmets. Released in 2013, it blends electronic sounds with live instruments and styles drawn from disco and funk. The album includes the hit “Get Lucky,” featuring singer Pharrell Williams and guitarist Nile Rodgers, as well as “Lose Yourself to Dance” and the multi-part track “Touch.” Another track, “Giorgio by Moroder,” begins with pioneering Italian producer Giorgio Moroder speaking about his early career while the instrumental music gradually builds around his voice. Moroder helped shape electronic dance music and worked with Donna Summer on her influential song “I Feel Love.” These collaborations helped Daft Punk connect the history of dance music with their own sound.

Darwin Watterson is a main character in the Cartoon Network series The Amazing World of Gumball. He is an orange goldfish with legs who lives with the Watterson family as Gumball’s adopted younger brother. Gumball is a blue cat, and the two brothers are close friends as well as frequent partners in unusual adventures. Darwin’s cheerful, loyal nature often balances Gumball’s more impulsive ideas. Their hometown is the fictional town of Elmore, where they go to school and meet a colorful mix of people, animals, and talking objects. The show makes Elmore especially distinctive by drawing its characters in many different animation styles. In the episode “The Boredom,” Gumball and Darwin even wander around town looking for an adventure.

Chris Pine is an American actor best known for playing Captain James T. Kirk in the Star Trek reboot films, beginning with Star Trek in 2009 and continuing in Star Trek Into Darkness and Star Trek Beyond. Kirk commands the starship Enterprise, and his friendship with Spock, a half-human, half-Vulcan officer played by Zachary Quinto, is central to the films. Pine also plays Steve Trevor, a pilot and ally of Wonder Woman, opposite Gal Gadot in Wonder Woman and Wonder Woman 1984. In the thriller Don’t Worry Darling, he appeared alongside singer and actor Harry Styles. Pine’s roles in both the Star Trek and Wonder Woman films have made him a familiar face in science-fiction and superhero movies.

The 1930s were the years from 1930 to 1939. In the United States, the Great Depression caused widespread unemployment and hardship, while President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal introduced programs intended to provide relief and help the economy recover. Music offered entertainment during these difficult years: swing and big-band recordings became widely popular, including Glenn Miller’s “In the Mood.” Broadway musicals also produced lasting hits. Cole Porter wrote “You’re the Top” for the musical Anything Goes and composed “Begin the Beguine” and “Night and Day.” His songs later became jazz standards performed by singers such as Ella Fitzgerald, known as the “First Lady of Song” and for her scat singing. Blues singer Bessie Smith died in 1937, placing her death in the same decade.

Silent films are motion pictures made without synchronized recorded dialogue. They often used written intertitles, or title cards, to show what characters said or to explain parts of the story. Actors also relied on facial expressions and gestures to help audiences follow the action, while music was often played during screenings. Silent films flourished before synchronized sound became standard and “talkies” such as The Jazz Singer grew popular in the late 1920s. One landmark silent film is Sergei Eisenstein’s 1925 Soviet film Battleship Potemkin. It dramatizes a 1905 mutiny by Russian sailors and is especially famous for its Odessa Steps sequence, in which a baby carriage rolls down a staircase. Eisenstein used montage—editing shots together to create an effect—to make the scene powerful.

Montage is a film-editing technique that joins separate shots into a sequence so that their order and contrast create meaning, associations, or dramatic effects. Early Soviet filmmakers explored how editing could shape what audiences think and feel. In Sergei Eisenstein’s silent film Battleship Potemkin, quick cuts between people fleeing down the Odessa Steps and a baby carriage rolling down them heighten the scene’s tension. A related idea is the Kuleshov effect, named after filmmaker Lev Kuleshov: viewers may read different emotions into the same unchanged shot of an actor’s face depending on the image placed beside it. Paired with a bowl of soup, the face might seem hungry; paired with a coffin, it might seem sad. The meaning comes from the shots together, not just from either shot alone.

MrBeast is the stage name of Jimmy Donaldson, an American YouTuber and entrepreneur known for videos featuring elaborate challenges, expensive stunts, and large cash giveaways. In 2020, he launched MrBeast Burger, a virtual restaurant brand. Instead of opening its own conventional dining rooms, the brand worked with existing restaurant kitchens to prepare orders placed through delivery apps. This arrangement is often called a ghost kitchen: customers order online for delivery or pickup, while the food may be cooked inside a restaurant operating under a different name. Ghost kitchens became especially common during the COVID-19 pandemic, when demand for food delivery grew. MrBeast Burger shows how an online creator can use a large audience to promote a food business without relying on traditional restaurant locations.

The Blair Witch Project is a 1999 horror film that tells its story through “found footage”: recordings supposedly recovered after three student filmmakers disappear. Heather, Mike, and Josh travel to Burkittsville, Maryland, to make a documentary about the local legend of the Blair Witch. They interview residents, then hike into the nearby Black Hills Forest to investigate. As they become lost, they hear frightening sounds at night and find strange signs in the woods. Heather and Mike wonder whether screams outside their tent are a trick meant to lure them out. The film rarely shows what might be pursuing them, relying instead on shaky camera footage and the students’ growing fear to make the story feel real.

The New York Post is an American newspaper founded in 1801 by Alexander Hamilton, a prominent figure in the early United States. It was later acquired by media owner Rupert Murdoch. The paper is especially known for attention-grabbing headlines and celebrity coverage, including its Page Six gossip section and website. One famous front-page headline read “Headless Body in Topless Bar.” The Post is often called a tabloid. A tabloid is a compact newspaper traditionally folded once along a vertical spine, unlike a larger broadsheet. The word also often describes a style of journalism that emphasizes dramatic stories, gossip, and sensational headlines. Not every story in a tabloid is about celebrities, but its bold presentation is designed to catch readers’ attention.

The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum opened in 1995 on the Lake Erie waterfront in Cleveland, Ohio. It preserves the history of rock and roll and related popular music through exhibits of recordings, instruments, costumes, and other objects. Its Hall of Fame honors influential performers and music-industry figures, including the Beatles, Aretha Franklin, and Tina Turner. The building is a landmark too: its glass pyramid and bold geometric shapes were designed by Chinese-American architect I. M. Pei. He also designed the glass pyramid outside the Louvre Museum in Paris, an art museum that houses works such as the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo.

The PlayStation 5, often called the PS5, is a Sony home video game console released in 2020 as the successor to the PlayStation 4. Its distinctive white-and-black shell makes it easy to recognize, while its high-speed solid-state drive, or SSD, helps games load quickly. Launch games included Marvel’s Spider-Man: Miles Morales, and the console is also known for Horizon Forbidden West. The PS5 launched with a wireless controller called the DualSense. Unlike earlier PlayStation controllers, it has adaptive triggers that can change how much resistance you feel when pressing them, as well as haptic feedback that produces different sensations to match events in a game. The DualSense also has a two-tone design and a built-in microphone.

She-Ra and the Princesses of Power is a Netflix animated fantasy series about Adora, a young soldier raised by the Horde, an army trying to conquer her world. After finding a magical sword in the Whispering Woods, Adora learns that she can transform into the powerful warrior She-Ra. She leaves the Horde and joins a group of magical princesses to fight it. Their home planet is called Etheria, and many of the princesses draw their elemental powers from ancient runestones found across it. The series explores friendship and loyalty as Adora faces former friends on the opposing side, including Catra. This version reimagines She-Ra, a character first introduced in 1985 as He-Man’s twin sister.

Tom Nook is a recurring character in Animal Crossing, Nintendo’s life-simulation video game series. He is a tanuki-like entrepreneur who has worked as a shopkeeper and helps players finance their homes and later expansions. Players repay these loans in Bells, the series’ in-game currency, which they can also use to buy furniture and other items. Animal Crossing lets players decorate their homes, collect resources, and get to know a community of anthropomorphic animal villagers. Rather than following a single fixed story, players build a life in their town or island at their own pace. In Animal Crossing: New Horizons, released in March 2020, Tom Nook helps the player begin a new life on a deserted island.

Crabcore is an internet-era label for a performance style associated with some late-2000s metalcore bands. Musicians would crouch low with their legs spread wide, torsos leaning forward, and arms bent outward, making them look a little like crabs. The term describes the pose and the online attention it received, rather than a separate kind of music. Ohio band Attack Attack! became a famous example after its video for “Stick Stickly” spread online; the song appeared on the band’s 2008 debut album, Someday Came Suddenly. Abandon All Ships was another band linked to the label. Both bands mixed heavy metalcore sounds with electronic effects and Auto-Tune, helping make the style especially recognizable to internet audiences.

CNN, short for Cable News Network, is an American cable television network launched by Ted Turner in 1980. It became the first television channel devoted to news coverage 24 hours a day, allowing viewers to follow major events as they unfolded rather than waiting for a scheduled newscast. CNN is known for the motto “The Most Trusted Name in News” and for programs led by recognizable journalists. One of its longtime anchors is Wolf Blitzer, who presents The Situation Room, a show focused on breaking news and current events. Blitzer also appeared on a much-ridiculed episode of Jeopardy! in 2009, finishing with a negative score of $4,500. Despite that game-show result, he remains a well-known CNN journalist.

South by Southwest, often shortened to SXSW, is an annual festival and conference in Austin, Texas. It began in 1987 as a music event where performers could play for audiences and music-industry professionals. Over time, it expanded to include film screenings, talks, and interactive-media programming focused on subjects such as technology and digital culture. Today, SXSW brings together musicians, filmmakers, creators, and visitors for performances, premieres, and discussions. Its host city, Austin, is the capital of Texas and the seat of Travis County. Austin lies along the Colorado River and is known for its live-music scene, making it a fitting home for a festival that started with music and grew to cover many forms of entertainment and media.

Nightwing is the superhero identity Dick Grayson adopted after he outgrew his role as Robin, Batman’s young acrobatic partner. Raised in a circus family, Dick used his athletic skills to fight crime alongside Batman in Gotham City. As he grew older, he wanted to become a hero in his own right rather than remain Batman’s sidekick. He chose the name Nightwing and eventually made Blüdhaven, a crime-ridden port city near Gotham, his primary base. There he faced dangerous criminals, including Roland Desmond, a powerful crime boss known as Blockbuster. Dick still works with Batman and other heroes, but as Nightwing he makes his own decisions and protects a city that depends on him.

James Cameron is a Canadian filmmaker known for ambitious action and science-fiction movies, including The Terminator, Aliens, The Abyss, Titanic, and Avatar. His films often feature advanced technology and people facing extreme environments. Titanic tells a fictional love story aboard the luxury liner that sank after striking an iceberg, while Avatar is set on Pandora, a moon where humans seek a valuable mineral. Cameron’s interest in underwater exploration extends beyond filmmaking. In 2012, he piloted a specially designed submersible called the Deepsea Challenger on a solo descent to the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in the Mariana Trench. This voyage connected his work as a filmmaker with his fascination for exploring parts of the ocean that few people have ever seen.

Elden Ring is a 2022 open-world action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment. Players explore a vast fantasy realm called the Lands Between, battling powerful enemies and uncovering its history as they work toward becoming the Elden Lord. The game is known for its challenging combat, freedom to explore, and mysterious story. Its worldbuilding was developed with input from American author George R. R. Martin, best known for the epic fantasy book series A Song of Ice and Fire, which inspired the television show Game of Thrones. One famous Elden Ring player, known as “Let Me Solo Her,” became popular for helping others defeat the difficult boss Malenia, Blade of Miquella, while wearing a pot on his head.

Remember the Titans is a 2000 American sports drama based on the true story of the newly integrated American football team at T.C. Williams High School in Alexandria, Virginia. Set in 1971, it follows Black and white players learning to work together during a time of racial tension. Denzel Washington plays Herman Boone, the team’s head coach, while Will Patton plays Bill Yoast, a former head coach who becomes Boone’s assistant and defensive coordinator. Their cooperation helps the players build trust on and off the field. The film shows how the team’s shared goal of winning games challenges prejudice in the school and community. Although it is based on real people and events, some details were changed for the movie.

The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles are four mutant turtle brothers who walk and talk like humans and fight crime using ninjutsu. Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird introduced them in a 1984 independent comic published through Mirage Studios. The brothers are named after Renaissance artists: Leonardo, Donatello, Michelangelo, and Raphael. They live in New York City’s sewers, where a mutant rat named Splinter raises them and teaches them ninjutsu. Splinter is both their father figure and their sensei, or teacher. Often called TMNT, the turtles became stars of animated shows, movies, and video games, including The Cowabunga Collection, which brings together thirteen older games. Their adventures often pit them against villains such as Bebop, Rocksteady, and Krang.

The LEGO Movie is a 2014 computer-animated comedy set in a world built from LEGO bricks. Its main character, Emmet Brickowski, is an ordinary construction-worker minifigure who discovers a powerful artifact called the Piece of Resistance. He is mistaken for “the Special,” a hero prophesied to stop Lord Business, a ruler who wants to impose strict order on the LEGO world. Emmet joins the Master Builders, creative characters who can turn ordinary bricks into almost anything, to resist Lord Business’s plan. The elderly Master Builder Vitruvius, voiced by Morgan Freeman, is the one who foretells the Special’s arrival. The film combines action and jokes with a story about creativity and working together, and its upbeat song “Everything Is Awesome” became especially well known.

The Wachowskis are sisters Lana and Lilly Wachowski, the filmmakers who created the 1999 science-fiction film The Matrix. Its story follows Neo, a hacker who discovers that the world he knows is a computer simulation and joins a resistance fighting the machines behind it. The sisters continued shaping the franchise through the sequels The Matrix Reloaded and The Matrix Revolutions. When the series returned with The Matrix Resurrections in 2021, Lana directed it without Lilly. Keanu Reeves reprised his role as Neo in that film. Reeves is also known for starring in the John Wick action films and for playing Ted in the Bill & Ted movies.

Batman is the masked identity of Bruce Wayne, a wealthy heir in Gotham City who decided to fight crime after witnessing the murder of his parents as a child. Unlike many DC Comics heroes, Batman has no superpowers. He relies on detective skills, martial arts, and specialized gadgets, earning the nickname “the Caped Crusader.” His stories appear in comics, films, and other media. In the 1995 film Batman Forever, Val Kilmer plays Batman opposite Jim Carrey as the Riddler. This puzzle-obsessed villain leaves riddles for Batman while developing a device that can read minds. Crossword editor Will Shortz created the Riddler’s puzzle clues for the film.

Seven Samurai is a 1954 Japanese film directed by Akira Kurosawa. It follows a struggling farming village whose crops are threatened by bandits planning to return at harvest time. Unable to defend themselves, the villagers recruit seven masterless samurai, warriors without lords, to protect them. The samurai train the villagers and fight alongside them, but their victory comes at a cost. In the final scene, the surviving fighters stand near graves marked with swords while the villagers return to planting, showing how life in the village continues after the battle. Kurosawa was an influential filmmaker who also directed Rashomon, which brought Japanese cinema new international attention, and Throne of Blood, an adaptation of Shakespeare’s Macbeth.

Jurassic Park is a science fiction film franchise about dinosaurs brought back through genetic engineering and the dangers of turning them into attractions. It began with the 1993 film Jurassic Park, directed by Steven Spielberg and adapted from Michael Crichton’s novel. In that film, wealthy businessman John Hammond invites visitors to preview his dinosaur theme park on Isla Nublar, a fictional island off Costa Rica. When the park’s security systems fail, the visitors must survive encounters with escaped dinosaurs. Later films continue the story, including the Jurassic World movies, which feature a successor resort built on Isla Nublar. Across the franchise, scientists, park staff, and visitors face the consequences of trying to control prehistoric animals.

Rod Serling was an American television and radio writer who became famous for stories that used suspense and surprising twists to explore human behavior. His 1955 Kraft Television Theatre episode “Patterns” portrayed a ruthless struggle for power at a corporation, including a boardroom confrontation that leads to an older employee’s heart attack. The acclaimed drama helped establish Serling’s reputation as a screenwriter. He later created and hosted The Twilight Zone, an anthology series in which each episode told a different science-fiction, fantasy, or horror story. Its characters were often ordinary people facing strange or unsettling events. Serling introduced episodes with a narration describing “a fifth dimension beyond that which is known to man,” inviting viewers into the mysterious world of The Twilight Zone.

Lizzo is the stage name of Melissa Viviane Jefferson, an American singer, rapper, songwriter, and flutist. She became widely known through the 2019 hit “Truth Hurts,” which reached No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart. Her music mixes pop, hip-hop, R&B, and dance sounds, often with upbeat messages about confidence and self-acceptance. In 2022, she released the album Special, which includes “2 Be Loved (Am I Ready).” Its disco-influenced lead single, “About Damn Time,” features the lyric about needing a “sentimental man or woman to pump me up.” The song became Lizzo’s second Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 after “Truth Hurts.” Lizzo is also a skilled flute player and performed on a crystal flute once owned by President James Madison in 2022.

“Psycho Killer” is a 1977 song by Talking Heads, a New York rock band known for mixing punk and new wave sounds. It appeared on their debut album, Talking Heads: 77, and became one of their signature recordings. The song’s tense rhythm and David Byrne’s uneasy vocal performance create the feeling of an anxious narrator. One of its most memorable moments is the repeated French question “qu’est-ce que c’est,” meaning “what is it?”, followed by the urgent phrase “run, run, run away.” The band’s original core trio was singer and guitarist David Byrne, bassist Tina Weymouth, and drummer Chris Frantz. Keyboardist and guitarist Jerry Harrison joined later, completing the group’s best-known lineup.

Film is a visual medium that uses a sequence of recorded images to create the appearance of motion, usually with sound, to tell stories or present information. Individual works are called films, movies, or motion pictures, and many are screened in theaters such as AMC and Cinemark. Films have been shaped by industry rules: the Hays Code was an early American set of guidelines that restricted what movies could show, while modern U.S. motion-picture ratings include PG-13, R, and NC-17. Film festivals celebrate filmmaking and bring attention to new work. Sundance is especially known for independent, or “indie,” films. At the annual Cannes Film Festival in France, the highest prize is the Palme d’Or, meaning “Golden Palm.” First awarded in 1955, it is named for the festival’s golden palm emblem.

Emma Frost is a Marvel Comics mutant known for her powerful telepathy: she can read minds and communicate through thought. She can also transform her body into durable organic diamond, which protects her from physical harm. Frost was once the White Queen of the Hellfire Club, a group that often opposed the X-Men, but she later became an important member of the X-Men herself. She also began a relationship with Scott Summers, the X-Men leader known as Cyclops. Five young telepaths—Sophie, Irma, Celeste, Esme, and Phoebe—were cloned from Emma Frost. Together, the sisters are called the Stepford Cuckoos. Their shared origin and telepathic powers connect them closely to Frost’s story.

Blade Runner is a 1982 science-fiction film directed by Ridley Scott and starring Harrison Ford as Rick Deckard, a former police officer assigned to hunt down escaped artificial humans called replicants. Its dark, rain-soaked setting imagines a future in which replicants are created to work for humans, often on off-world colonies. One of them, Roy Batty, is a Nexus-6 replicant played by Rutger Hauer. After escaping a colony, Roy searches for his maker, hoping to extend his short lifespan. Near the end of the film, he reflects on his extraordinary memories in a famous speech known as “Tears in Rain,” then dies. The film uses Deckard’s pursuit of Roy and the other replicants to ask what makes someone human.

Arthur is a PBS Kids animated series about Arthur Read, a bespectacled fourth-grade aardvark growing up in the fictional city of Elwood City. Through Arthur’s adventures with his younger sister D.W., his best friend Buster Baxter, and their classmates and families, the show explores friendship, school, and everyday challenges. Their teacher, Mr. Ratburn, is also an important character; in the episode “Mr. Ratburn and the Special Someone,” he marries his husband, Patrick. Another episode, “The Boy Who Cried Comet,” has characters worried that a comet seen through a telescope will hit Earth. The television series was adapted from books created by American author and illustrator Marc Brown. He introduced Arthur in Arthur’s Nose, published in 1976.

The Nintendo Switch is a video game system released in 2017 that works both as a home console and as a portable handheld. Players can place it in a dock to play on a television, then lift it out to continue playing on its built-in screen. Its detachable Joy-Con controllers can also be shared for multiplayer games away from the TV. The Switch hosts many games, including titles in the Pokémon franchise, which began with Pokémon Red and Blue and features characters such as Pikachu and Charizard. In 2021, Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl and Pokémon Legends: Arceus were announced for the Switch. Pokémon Legends: Arceus is an action role-playing game set in Hisui, an ancient version of Sinnoh, the region featured in the fourth generation’s Pokémon Diamond and Pearl.

Charli XCX is an English singer-songwriter and producer known for catchy pop songs and adventurous electronic sounds. Her stage name comes from her childhood online nickname, and her birth name is Charlotte Emma Aitchison. Her hit “Boom Clap” appears in the 2014 film The Fault in Our Stars, playing as the main characters, Hazel and Augustus, arrive in Amsterdam. In 2020, Charli XCX created the album How I’m Feeling Now during the COVID-19 lockdown. She involved fans in the creative process by sharing work in progress online and asking for their feedback. The album includes the songs “claws” and “forever” and explores the emotions and relationships she experienced while staying at home.

AC/DC is an Australian hard rock band famous for loud electric guitars, driving rhythms, and songs such as “Highway to Hell” and “Thunderstruck.” Guitarist Angus Young is known for playing energetic riffs that help give the band its distinctive sound. “Highway to Hell” appeared in 1979, when Bon Scott was the lead singer. After Scott died in 1980, Brian Johnson joined the band and sang on its next studio album, Back in Black. Released that same year, Back in Black includes the title track and “You Shook Me All Night Long.” AC/DC’s music has also inspired other performers: the Croatian duo 2CELLOS created a fast-paced cello version of “Thunderstruck” and covered several other AC/DC songs.

James Bond is a fictional British spy created by author Ian Fleming. He works for MI6, Britain’s foreign intelligence service, and is known by his service number, 007. Bond first appeared in Fleming’s 1953 novel Casino Royale, in which he travels to a French gaming resort to face Le Chiffre, an enemy agent, at baccarat. Bond’s mission is to bankrupt Le Chiffre by winning at the card game. Bond is also the protagonist of Moonraker, another Fleming novel, in which he investigates Hugo Drax and a dangerous weapons project. Fleming wrote many Bond stories, and the character later became famous through films as well as books. Other authors, including John Gardner, have continued the novel series.

Peter O’Toole was an Irish-born actor whose international breakthrough came when he played British officer T. E. Lawrence in David Lean’s 1962 epic Lawrence of Arabia. Set during the First World War, the film follows Lawrence as he helps unite Arab tribes in a revolt against Ottoman rule. Its sweeping desert cinematography made it especially famous. O’Toole later earned Academy Award nominations for portraying England’s King Henry II in two different films, Becket and The Lion in Winter. His career also included voice acting: he played Anton Ego, a hard-to-please food critic, in Pixar’s Ratatouille, an animated film about a rat who dreams of becoming a chef.

Aurora Aksnes, who performs as AURORA, is a Norwegian singer-songwriter known for art-pop music that blends electronic sounds with expressive vocals. Her songs “Runaway” and “Running with the Wolves” both appear on her 2016 debut studio album, All My Demons Greeting Me as a Friend. “Runaway” helped introduce many listeners to her music, while “Running with the Wolves” shows her imaginative style. AURORA also contributed backing vocals as a mysterious voice heard by Elsa in “Into the Unknown” from the animated film Frozen II. Elsa’s main vocals in that song are sung by Idina Menzel, but AURORA’s distinctive voice helps make its haunting call memorable.

Orson Welles was an American actor, director, writer, and producer who helped change how stories were told on screen and radio. In his 1941 film Citizen Kane, he directed and starred as newspaper tycoon Charles Foster Kane, whose dying word, “Rosebud,” leads others to investigate his life. Welles also played corrupt police captain Hank Quinlan in the film noir Touch of Evil, which opens with a long tracking shot of a car carrying a bomb. His later essay film F for Fake explores art, forgery, and deception. Before these films, Welles and his Mercury Theatre on the Air presented a 1938 radio adaptation of H. G. Wells’s alien-invasion novel. Using simulated news bulletins about objects landing in New Jersey, it became known as The War of the Worlds broadcast.

The Simpsons is a long-running American animated sitcom about a family living in the fictional town of Springfield. Homer Simpson works at a nuclear power plant, while his son Bart is famous for mischievous pranks. The family also includes Marge, Lisa, and baby Maggie. Much of the show’s humor comes from their everyday lives and the unusual people around them. Their next-door neighbor, Ned Flanders, is a cheerful evangelical Christian who often greets people with “Hi-diddly-ho.” He stays remarkably patient with Homer, even when Homer treats him badly. Each year, the show’s “Treehouse of Horror” episodes tell separate, spooky stories that parody horror, science fiction, and fantasy. Some feature the aliens Kang and Kodos and make playful references to shows such as The Twilight Zone.

Bridgerton is a Netflix period-romance series produced by Shondaland and adapted from Julia Quinn’s novels. Set in Regency-era London, it follows the wealthy and influential Bridgerton family as its members search for love while navigating the rules, gossip, and expectations of high society. Much of the drama unfolds during the social season, when young people attend balls and other events in hopes of making advantageous marriages. An anonymous writer known as Lady Whistledown reports on the society’s secrets, adding to the pressure on the families involved. Golda Rosheuvel plays Queen Charlotte, the monarch who presides over the social season and takes a keen interest in the debutantes seeking suitable matches.

Attaway General is a scripted teen drama about young volunteers working at a hospital. It was distributed on Hulu Plus and YouTube and drew harsh reviews, with critics questioning its acting and storytelling. The show’s cast included Lauren Kettering and Madi Monroe, who were already known as social-media personalities. In one episode, a volunteer named Kit organizes a prom for Holden before he undergoes heart surgery. Much of the attention around Attaway General came from its connection to TikTok, the short-form video app owned by the Chinese company ByteDance. Several cast members had built audiences there before appearing on the show. Some TikTok creators were also associated with the Hype House, a Los Angeles group whose members made videos together.

Guns N’ Roses is an American hard rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1985. Singer Axl Rose and guitarist Slash are two of its best-known members. The band’s name combines “guns” with “roses,” flowers often associated with romance. Its powerful guitar riffs and energetic performances helped make it one of the most famous rock bands of the late 1980s. Guns N’ Roses released its debut studio album, Appetite for Destruction, in 1987. That album includes three of the band’s best-known songs: “Welcome to the Jungle,” “Paradise City,” and “Sweet Child o’ Mine.” If you hear those song titles together in a question, they may be clues to either the band Guns N’ Roses or its first album, Appetite for Destruction.

The Legend of Zelda is Nintendo’s long-running action-adventure series about Link, a hero who explores the kingdom of Hyrule, solves dungeon puzzles, and battles monsters to protect Princess Zelda and others. A recurring enemy is Ganondorf, a powerful Gerudo who seeks the Triforce, a magical source of power. In the 1998 Nintendo 64 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Link travels between childhood and adulthood, including a seven-year jump, to stop Ganondorf. The game also popularized lock-on targeting, which helps players focus on an enemy during combat. The 2017 open-world game The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild begins with Link awakening after a century of sleep and lets players explore Hyrule freely.

Andy Warhol is best known for Pop Art images such as his Campbell’s soup cans and Marilyn Monroe portraits, but he also made more than 100 experimental films. Instead of telling conventional stories, many of these films hold the camera on an ordinary subject for an unusually long time, inviting viewers to notice small changes and think about how they watch movies. His 1963 film Sleep shows poet John Giorno asleep in bed for roughly five hours. Another famous work, Empire, presents about eight hours of slow-motion footage of the Empire State Building. These long films challenged audiences’ expectations of what a movie could be: everyday scenes became the main event rather than the background to a plot.

In Ridley Scott’s 1979 science-fiction horror film Alien, the crew of the spaceship Nostromo encounters a dangerous extraterrestrial organism after it attaches itself to crew member Kane’s face. The ship’s onboard computer, an artificial intelligence called Mother, has a secret directive known as Special Order 937. This order makes bringing the organism back for study the top priority, even if the crew dies. Mother communicates the order to Ash, the Nostromo’s science officer, without telling Ripley or the rest of the crew. Ash appears to be human, but he is later revealed to be an android: an artificial being designed to look and act like a person. The secret order helps explain why Ash puts the alien’s survival ahead of his crewmates’ safety.

Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them is a 2016 fantasy film set mainly in New York City in 1926. It follows Newt Scamander, a British magizoologist who studies and cares for magical creatures. When several creatures escape from his enchanted case, Newt must find them before they cause trouble or expose the hidden wizarding world. At a bank, Newt’s case is mistakenly switched with one belonging to Jacob Kowalski, a No-Maj, or person without magic, who hopes to open a bakery. Jacob becomes Newt’s friend and helps him and witch Tina Goldstein search for the creatures. The film’s title is also the title of a guidebook to magical creatures credited to Newt in the Harry Potter universe.

Jango Fett is an armored bounty hunter in Star Wars whose genetic material was used to create the Republic’s clone troopers. The army was secretly produced by cloners on Kamino, an ocean-covered planet where the cloning facilities were based in Tipoca City. While investigating an assassination attempt on Senator Padmé Amidala, Obi-Wan Kenobi traveled to Kamino, discovered the clone army, and fought Jango there. Jango later died at the hands of Jedi Master Mace Windu during the Battle of Geonosis. The clone troopers went on to fight Separatist droids in the Clone Wars as the Grand Army of the Republic. Although they shared Jango’s genetic template, some clones developed distinct personalities, and a mutated group became known as the Bad Batch.

Goodfellas is a 1990 crime film directed by Martin Scorsese. Based on the life of real mobster Henry Hill, it follows his rise in the Mafia and the collapse of the criminal life he once found exciting. Ray Liotta plays Hill, while Robert De Niro and Joe Pesci play men in his circle of organized crime. As Hill becomes involved in robberies, drugs, and violence, his choices put him and his family in danger. After he is arrested, Hill cooperates with prosecutors by giving evidence against other mobsters and enters witness protection. The film shows both the attraction of wealth and status in the mob and the fear and betrayal that come with it.

Tom Hanks is an American actor known for playing memorable characters in many popular films. In the 1994 movie Forrest Gump, he played the title character, a kind-hearted man whose life takes him through several major events in American history. Hanks also portrayed Geppetto in Disney’s 2022 live-action adaptation of Pinocchio. Geppetto is a woodcarver who creates a wooden puppet named Pinocchio and wishes for him to become a real boy. Pinocchio’s nose grows when he lies, but Geppetto cares for him as a father. If a question asks which actor played both Forrest Gump and Geppetto, the answer is Tom Hanks. If it asks for the name of the woodcarver Hanks played, the answer is Geppetto.

The Wall Street Journal is an American daily newspaper first published in 1889. Founded by Charles H. Dow and his colleagues, it became a signature publication of Dow Jones & Company. It is best known for reporting on business, finance, and financial markets, helping readers follow companies, the economy, and changes in stock prices. Its name refers to Wall Street, the New York City area closely associated with American finance, but the newspaper covers national and international news as well. In 2007, News Corporation acquired Dow Jones & Company, bringing The Wall Street Journal under the ownership of a company led by Rupert Murdoch, an Australian-born media proprietor.

42 is a 2013 biographical sports drama about Jackie Robinson, played by Chadwick Boseman. The title refers to Robinson’s jersey number. In 1947, Robinson made his major-league debut with the Brooklyn Dodgers, becoming the first Black player in the modern era of Major League Baseball. His arrival broke the league’s long-standing racial barrier, but he faced racist insults, threats, and unfair treatment on and off the field. Harrison Ford plays Branch Rickey, the Dodgers executive who signed Robinson and urged him to respond to hostility without fighting back. The film follows Robinson’s challenges during his first season and shows how his skill and courage helped change baseball. Boseman’s performance in 42 was a breakthrough role before he later played Black Panther in Marvel films.

“Sicko Mode” is a 2018 hip-hop track by Travis Scott featuring Drake. It appears on Astroworld, Scott’s third studio album. The album takes its name from a former amusement park in Scott’s hometown of Houston, Texas, which closed in 2005. Rather than following one steady instrumental pattern, “Sicko Mode” moves through several distinct sections with dramatic beat switches. Changes in rhythm and production give Drake’s and Scott’s verses different sounds while keeping them part of the same song. Those shifts helped make the track especially recognizable. If you are asked to identify the 2018 Astroworld song featuring Drake and known for beat switches, the answer is “Sicko Mode.” If you are asked which album contains the song, the answer is Astroworld.

EPCOT began as Walt Disney’s idea for a futuristic community, not a theme park. Its name stood for “Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow,” and Disney imagined it as a place to test new approaches to transportation, technology, and everyday urban life. After Walt died in 1966, his brother Roy helped move forward with Walt Disney World in Orlando, Florida, but the city was never built as planned. Instead, the EPCOT idea was reshaped into a theme park, which opened in 1982. Today, the park explores innovation and cultures from around the world. Its best-known landmark is a huge geodesic sphere near the entrance. Inside that sphere is Spaceship Earth, a ride that traces the history of human communication from early writing through modern digital technology.

GeoGuessr is an online geography game that drops players into an unfamiliar location shown through panoramic street-level images. Players look around for clues such as road signs, languages, buildings, vegetation, and landscapes, then place a marker on a world map to guess where they are. The closer the guess is to the actual location, the more points they earn. GeoGuessr’s standard interface uses imagery and maps from Google Maps, the online platform that also lets people search for businesses, get directions, and calculate driving routes. Its Street View feature provides the panoramic images that players inspect. Because Street View coverage varies around the world, some places appear in GeoGuessr much more often than others.

Claire Bloom is an English actress known for her work in theatre, film, and television. She appeared in Charlie Chaplin’s film Limelight and built a long career in both stage and screen roles. Bloom was married to the American novelist Philip Roth, who used parts of their relationship as inspiration for his fiction. In Roth’s novel I Married a Communist, the character Eve Frame is an actress modeled on Bloom. Eve writes a memoir about her marriage to Ira Ringold, a former radio star, revealing his Communist past. The character is fictional, so her actions in the novel should not be taken as a factual account of Bloom’s life. To remember the connection: Claire Bloom is the real actress, and Eve Frame is the character she inspired.

Back to the Future is a 1985 science-fiction film about Marty McFly, a teenager from Hill Valley who accidentally travels from 1985 to 1955 in a time machine built from a DeLorean car. The machine was invented by the eccentric Emmett “Doc” Brown. In the past, Marty accidentally interferes with his parents’ first meeting, putting his own existence at risk. He must help them meet and fall in love at their school’s Enchantment Under the Sea dance, where he also performs “Johnny B. Goode.” To get Marty home, Doc uses a predicted lightning strike at Hill Valley’s clock tower to supply the power the DeLorean needs. The film combines time-travel adventure with comedy about families and the differences between generations.

“Piano Man” is a 1973 song written and performed by New York-born singer-songwriter Billy Joel, who also recorded “Uptown Girl” and “New York State of Mind.” Before his breakthrough, Joel played piano at the Executive Room, a lounge in Los Angeles, under the name Bill Martin. His experiences there inspired “Piano Man”: the narrator plays for bar customers, listens to their stories, and takes requests for familiar music. As he sings about people hoping for a break from their troubles, the customers join in, telling him, “We’re all in the mood for a melody, and you’ve got us feeling alright.” The song’s characters and barroom setting helped make it one of Joel’s best-known recordings.

Chopped is a Food Network cooking competition in which four chefs must turn baskets of mystery ingredients into dishes under strict time limits. The baskets often contain foods that seem difficult to combine, so contestants need to think quickly and use their cooking skills creatively. They compete in three rounds—appetizer, entrée, and dessert—with a new basket for each round. After tasting the dishes, a panel of judges eliminates, or “chops,” one chef. The last chef remaining wins. One of the show’s judges, chef Scott Conant, is especially known for his strong dislike of raw onions in contestants’ dishes. Conant also hosted Chopped Sweets, a spinoff that focused on desserts.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a 1998 action-adventure video game in Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda series. Players control Link, a young hero exploring the kingdom of Hyrule to stop the villain Ganondorf. When Link draws the sacred Master Sword from its pedestal, he is sealed away and awakens seven years later to find that Ganondorf has taken control. Link travels between his childhood and adult years, solves puzzles in temples, and plays melodies on the magical Ocarina of Time. As an adult, he meets a mysterious masked Sheikah named Sheik, who teaches him songs that help him travel to distant locations. Near the end of the story, Sheik reveals that she is Princess Zelda in disguise.

Naruto is a Japanese anime series about Naruto Uzumaki, a young ninja who dreams of becoming the leader of his village. He uses techniques such as the Rasengan, a powerful spinning ball of energy, and the shadow clone technique, which creates copies of himself. Another important young ninja is Sasuke Uchiha, Naruto’s teammate and rival. Sasuke belongs to the Uchiha clan, whose members can inherit a special sight ability called the Sharingan. His older brother, Itachi, carried out a massacre of their clan, leaving Sasuke determined to grow stronger and confront him. These characters and their abilities are central to the story of Naruto.

The Skeld is the first map in Among Us, a social deduction game created by Innersloth. It is set aboard a spacecraft where crewmates try to finish tasks while impostors secretly hunt them and sabotage the ship. The Cafeteria sits near the top of the map, while Reactor and Security are on the left side. In Admin, a crewmate might complete a card-swipe task, but an impostor can only pretend to do it. Impostors can also use venting: they disappear through floor grates and travel to connected grates elsewhere on the ship. Crewmates normally cannot do this, but those assigned the Engineer role can use the vents too. If players suspect someone is an impostor, they can call an emergency meeting and vote to eject a player into space.

“Almost (Sweet Music)” is a 2019 song by Irish singer-songwriter Hozier. It appears as the second track on his second studio album, Wasteland, Baby!, immediately after “Nina Cried Power.” The album also includes “Movement,” “Nobody,” and “Dinner & Diatribes.” In “Almost (Sweet Music),” Hozier uses references to classic jazz standards and jazz musicians’ songs to tell a romantic story. The title’s word “Sweet” connects it to other familiar song titles, including Eurythmics’ “Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)” and Neil Diamond’s “Sweet Caroline,” but those are separate songs. If asked for Hozier’s full song title, include the parentheses: “Almost (Sweet Music).” The album title is Wasteland, Baby!, including the comma and exclamation point.

Encanto is a 2021 Walt Disney Animation Studios musical set in Colombia. It follows the Madrigal family, who live in an enchanted house called the Casita. A magical candle gives most family members special gifts, such as super strength or the ability to control the weather, but Mirabel has no gift of her own. When the house’s magic begins to fail, Mirabel tries to discover why and help her family. Her uncle Bruno Madrigal can see visions of the future. After a troubling vision involving Mirabel, he disappears, and the family avoids talking about him in the song “We Don’t Talk About Bruno.” Another song, “Surface Pressure,” reveals how Mirabel’s strong sister Luisa feels burdened by everyone’s expectations.

Stand by Me is a 1986 coming-of-age drama directed by Rob Reiner and adapted from Stephen King’s novella The Body. Set in the fictional town of Castle Rock, Oregon, it follows four friends who hike into the woods after hearing where the body of a missing boy might be found. The journey becomes more than an adventure: as they face danger and talk about their lives, the boys learn about friendship, fear, and growing up. Wil Wheaton and River Phoenix are among the young cast. Although King is best known for horror stories, this film focuses on the boys’ relationships rather than supernatural scares. Reiner had previously directed the mockumentary This Is Spinal Tap and later directed the romantic comedy When Harry Met Sally....

Toy Story is a 1995 Pixar film and the first feature-length movie made entirely with computer animation. It follows toys that come to life when people are not watching. Woody, a cowboy doll, has long been the favorite toy of a boy named Andy, but he feels threatened when Andy receives a new space ranger toy, Buzz Lightyear. Their rivalry turns into a friendship as they try to get home after being separated from Andy. During their adventure, Woody and Buzz visit Pizza Planet, a fictional restaurant with an arcade claw machine full of little green alien toys. The Pizza Planet delivery truck later became a recurring Easter egg, or hidden reference, in Pixar films.

Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb is a 1964 black comedy directed by Stanley Kubrick. It uses absurd humor to show how nuclear weapons and military mistakes could threaten the entire world. The crisis begins when U.S. Air Force General Jack D. Ripper orders a nuclear attack without authorization. The President and his advisers gather in the War Room, trying to stop the bombers before they trigger global annihilation. Peter Sellers plays several characters, including Dr. Strangelove, a wheelchair-using former Nazi scientist who cannot control his Nazi salute. In one famous scene, Major Kong rides a falling nuclear bomb like a cowboy. Kubrick carefully designed the film’s imposing War Room; he also directed 2001: A Space Odyssey and A Clockwork Orange.

In Frank Herbert’s Dune universe, spice, also called melange, is a valuable substance found in the sands of the desert planet Arrakis. The planet’s native Fremen also call it Rakis. Large machines called crawlers harvest spice, but the work is dangerous because giant sandworms roam the desert. Spice affects the mind and can give regular users blue eyes.
